meta.title: Basic Banking Operations
meta.description: 400 MCQs covering 9 modules – The Business of Banking, Customer Service, Cash & Teller, Clearing, Treasury, Funds Transfer, E‑Banking, Foreign Operations, and Fraud.

questionBank.q: According to BOFIA 2020, which activity is specifically included in the definition of 'banking business'?
opts: A. Issuing commercial papers to the public.
B. Receiving deposits on current accounts.
C. Underwriting corporate bonds for clients.
questionBank.ans: B. Receiving deposits on current accounts.
questionBank.exp: BOFIA 2020 defines banking business as 'the business of receiving deposits on current accounts, savings accounts or other similar accounts, paying or collecting cheques, or any business as the CBN Governor may designate.' (Module 1, §1.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five main roles of banks in the global economy?
questionBank.exp: The five roles are intermediation, payment, guarantor, agency, and policy. Investment banking is not listed as one of the primary roles. (Module 1, §1.2)

questionBank.q: A customer deposits a valuable painting with a bank for safekeeping. This relationship is best described as:
questionBank.exp: When a customer transfers valuable items to a bank for safekeeping without transfer of ownership, the bank acts as a bailee and the customer as bailor. (Module 1, §1.8)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an example of a support group within a bank?
questionBank.exp: Support groups include Data Centre, Operations, Financial Control, Credit Administration, Legal, Human Resources, and Internal Control. Commercial, Private, and Corporate Banking are business groups. (Module 1, §1.7.2)

questionBank.q: A bank that consistently refuses to pay a customer's properly drawn cheques despite sufficient funds may be liable for:
opts: B. Breach of the duty to pay according to instructions.
C. Breach of the duty to provide a statement.
D. Exercising an improper right of set-off.
questionBank.ans: B. Breach of the duty to pay according to instructions.
questionBank.exp: The banker must make payments as the customer has authorised (up to the credit balance or agreed overdraft). Unjustified refusal can injure the customer's reputation and cause loss. (Module 1, §1.9.6)

questionBank.q: In the case of Tournier v National Provincial & Union Bank of England, which exception to the duty of confidentiality was established?
opts: D. All of the above are exceptions.
questionBank.ans: D. All of the above are exceptions.
questionBank.exp: The Tournier case established four exceptions: compulsion of law, public duty, interest of the bank, and express or implied consent of the customer. (Module 1, §1.9.7)

questionBank.q: A banker's right to combine a customer's credit balance with an overdrawn account in the same name is called:
questionBank.exp: The right of set-off allows the banker to net the customer's credit balance against his overdrawn account, provided both accounts are in the same name and right. (Module 1, §1.10.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a duty of the customer towards the bank?
opts: A. To provide a statement of account on request.
B. To exercise reasonable care when executing written orders.
C. To maintain confidentiality about the banker's affairs.
D. To pay a reasonable commission for services.
questionBank.ans: B. To exercise reasonable care when executing written orders.
questionBank.exp: The customer must exercise reasonable care in executing written orders so as not to mislead the bank or facilitate forgery. The other options are obligations of the bank. (Module 1, §1.11.1)

questionBank.q: A bank opens an account for a customer without verifying the customer's identity. A fraudster later uses the account to launder money. This is an example of:
opts: A. A failure to attend to account opening formalities.
B. A violation of the right of lien.
C. An error of commission in posting.
D. A breach of the duty to provide statements.
questionBank.ans: A. A failure to attend to account opening formalities.
questionBank.exp: The manual lists 'Failure to attend to account opening formalities, thereby enabling cheques to be more readily converted' as an act of negligence by banks. (Module 1, §1.13.1)

questionBank.q: Which principle of the CBN Consumer Protection Framework requires banks to provide accurate, timely, and clear information about products and services?
questionBank.exp: Disclosure and Transparency requires financial institutions to provide accurate information on products and services at all times to enable informed decisions. (Module 1, §1.14.1.3)

questionBank.q: A bank charges a customer a fee for issuing a cheque book. This fee falls under which category of bank income?
questionBank.exp: Commission and fees include charges for cheque books, funds transfer, collection, and other services. (Module 1, §1.16.2)

questionBank.q: A customer operates both a current account and a savings account with the same bank. When making a payment to the bank, the customer instructs that the payment be applied to the savings account. This is an exercise of the right of:
questionBank.exp: A customer with multiple accounts has the right to appropriate payment to whichever account he prefers, without duress from the bank. (Module 1, §1.11.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the trends affecting banks as listed in the manual?
questionBank.exp: Rising competition is listed as a trend, not decreasing competition. Other trends include service proliferation, deregulation, rising funding costs, and technology. (Module 1, §1.4)

questionBank.q: When a bank gives investment advice to a customer and the customer suffers a loss due to negligent advice, the bank may be liable under the duty of care owed in:
questionBank.exp: The duty of care owed in tort applies particularly where the bank gives investment advice. (Module 1, §1.8.6)

questionBank.q: A bank receives a cheque drawn by a customer that is post‑dated. Under the banker's duty to pay according to instructions, the bank should:
opts: A. Pay the cheque immediately if funds are available.
B. Return the cheque as post‑dated.
C. Hold the cheque until the date on the cheque and then pay.
D. Seek the customer's confirmation before paying.
questionBank.ans: B. Return the cheque as post‑dated.
questionBank.exp: A post‑dated cheque is not payable before its date; the bank should return it as irregular. The duty to pay only applies to properly drawn instruments. (Module 1, §1.9.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following best describes the 'payment role' of banks?
opts: A. Banks facilitate the transfer of funds between economic units.
B. Banks channel savings into investments.
C. Banks act as guarantors for their customers.
questionBank.ans: A. Banks facilitate the transfer of funds between economic units.
questionBank.exp: The payment role involves providing facilities for the transfer of funds. The intermediation role is channeling savings to investments. (Module 1, §1.2)

questionBank.q: A corporate customer requests a loan to purchase machinery. The bank's credit department approves the loan. This activity falls under which business group?
questionBank.exp: Corporate banking deals with banking services related to large companies or groups, including lending and financing. (Module 1, §1.7.1.iv)

questionBank.q: The principle of 'Fair Treatment' in the CBN Consumer Protection Framework requires that:
opts: A. Banks provide financial education to consumers.
B. Consumers be treated equitably without bias at all stages.
C. Consumer complaints be addressed within 24 hours.
D. Banks disclose all fees upfront.
questionBank.ans: B. Consumers be treated equitably without bias at all stages.
questionBank.exp: Fair treatment means consumers are treated equitably without bias, with equal access to basic services and consideration for vulnerable groups. (Module 1, §1.14.1.5)

questionBank.q: A bank's internal control department conducts a review to ensure compliance with the bank's Standard Operating Procedures. This falls under which support group?
opts: B. Internal Control or Internal Audit.
questionBank.ans: B. Internal Control or Internal Audit.
questionBank.exp: Internal Control or Internal Audit is responsible for checking compliance and adherence to SOPs. (Module 1, §1.7.2.vii)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an example of the right of lien exercised by a banker?
opts: A. Withholding a customer's share certificate until an outstanding loan is repaid.
B. Combining a customer's current account credit with an overdraft in a separate account.
C. Charging a fee for issuing a bank draft.
D. Refusing to pay a cheque because the account is dormant.
questionBank.ans: A. Withholding a customer's share certificate until an outstanding loan is repaid.
questionBank.exp: Lien is the right to retain or claim possession of a customer's property (movable or fixed) in the ordinary course of extending credit. Holding a share certificate until loan repayment is a lien. (Module 1, §1.10.2)

questionBank.q: A customer complains about a bank's failure to resolve an issue within a reasonable time. Which consumer protection principle requires banks to have effective complaints handling mechanisms that are affordable, fair, timely, transparent, accessible, and independent?
questionBank.exp: Complaints Handling and Redress requires adequate measures to address disputes, including affordable, fair, timely, transparent, accessible, and independent mechanisms. (Module 1, §1.14.1.7)

questionBank.q: In the banker‑customer relationship, when does a bank act as a trustee and beneficiary?
opts: A. When it holds money on a current account.
B. When it takes on a fiduciary role for a deceased's estate.
C. When it sells securities on behalf of a customer.
D. When it provides safe custody for valuables.
questionBank.ans: B. When it takes on a fiduciary role for a deceased's estate.
questionBank.exp: The bank acts as an administrator to a deceased's estate, which is a trustee‑beneficiary relationship. (Module 1, §1.8.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a basic service offered by banks as listed in the manual?
opts: B. Extension of credit facilities for trade.
questionBank.exp: Insurance underwriting is not listed; basic services include mobilization of savings, credit for trade, funds transfer, investment management, safe custody, brokerage, and foreign exchange facilities. (Module 1, §1.3)

questionBank.q: A bank refuses to provide a customer with a statement of account despite repeated requests. This is a breach of the bank's duty to:
opts: B. Provide a statement of account.
questionBank.ans: B. Provide a statement of account.
questionBank.exp: The bank has a duty to provide the customer on request with a statement of account. (Module 1, §1.9.8)

questionBank.q: Which of the following best describes the 'agency role' of banks?
opts: A. Banks act as intermediaries between savers and borrowers.
B. Banks execute transactions on behalf of customers.
C. Banks guarantee payment for their customers.
D. Banks implement government monetary policy.
questionBank.ans: B. Banks execute transactions on behalf of customers.
questionBank.exp: The agency role involves executing transactions on behalf of customers, such as buying and selling securities. (Module 1, §1.2.iv)

questionBank.q: A bank pays a forged cheque drawn on a customer's account. The customer had not been negligent. Under the banker's duty, the bank must:
opts: A. Refund the customer's account only if the customer complains.
B. Not refund because the customer failed to detect forgery.
C. Refund the customer's account and debit the loss.
D. Share the loss with the customer equally.
questionBank.ans: C. Refund the customer's account and debit the loss.
questionBank.exp: The bank must only make payments as authorized. A forged cheque is not authorized; the bank must refund the customer's account unless the customer's negligence contributed. (Module 1, §1.9.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a key objective of the CBN Consumer Protection Framework's 'Legal, Regulatory, and Supervisory Framework' principle?
opts: A. To ensure banks offer competitive interest rates.
B. To provide effective legal and regulatory structures to protect consumers.
C. To mandate financial literacy programmes for all customers.
D. To enforce prompt resolution of all complaints within 48 hours.
questionBank.ans: B. To provide effective legal and regulatory structures to protect consumers.
questionBank.exp: This principle requires that there shall be effective legal, regulatory, and supervisory structures to protect consumers. (Module 1, §1.14.1.1)

questionBank.q: A bank employee discloses a customer's account balance to a third party without the customer's consent, and the disclosure is not required by law. This is a breach of the banker's duty of:
questionBank.exp: The banker has a duty to keep customer affairs confidential, except in limited circumstances (Tournier exceptions). Unauthorised disclosure is a breach. (Module 1, §1.9.7)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an act of negligence by a bank?
opts: A. Collecting a cheque for an amount consistent with the customer's status.
B. Failing to obtain the name of a customer's employer during staff account opening.
C. Paying a cheque with an irregular endorsement after proper verification.
D. Returning a post‑dated cheque to the customer.
questionBank.ans: B. Failing to obtain the name of a customer's employer during staff account opening.
questionBank.exp: Failure to obtain the names of customer's employer during staff account opening is listed as an act of negligence. (Module 1, §1.13.2)

questionBank.q: What is the primary purpose of the 'Protection of Consumer Assets and Privacy' principle in the CBN framework?
opts: A. To ensure banks have adequate capital to cover losses.
B. To guarantee that consumer financial and personal information is protected.
C. To provide consumers with free credit reports.
D. To require banks to offer fraud insurance.
questionBank.ans: B. To guarantee that consumer financial and personal information is protected.
questionBank.exp: This principle requires that consumer's financial and personal information shall be protected and not released without consent, except as required by law. (Module 1, §1.14.1.6)

questionBank.q: A bank invests surplus funds in government securities. This activity is part of which role of banks?
questionBank.exp: The intermediation role involves channeling funds from savers to borrowers, including investment in securities. (Module 1, §1.2.i)

questionBank.q: A bank decides to close a customer's account without giving reasonable notice, while the customer still has outstanding cheques in circulation. This violates the banker's duty to:
opts: A. Provide a statement of account.
B. Not cease business without reasonable notice.
questionBank.ans: B. Not cease business without reasonable notice.
questionBank.exp: The bank must not cease to do business with the customer except upon reasonable notice, to allow time for outstanding cheques to be presented. (Module 1, §1.9.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a duty of the banker?
opts: A. To receive money and settle bills for the customer's account.
B. To lend money to the customer upon request.
C. To not cease business with the customer except upon reasonable notice.
D. To provide a statement of account on request.
questionBank.ans: B. To lend money to the customer upon request.
questionBank.exp: Lending is not a duty; it is a service the bank may offer. Duties include receiving money, repaying, giving notice, paying according to instructions, and providing statements. (Module 1, §1.9)

questionBank.q: When a bank collects a cheque drawn payable to a company and credits it to the personal account of the company's director without authorization, this is an act of:
questionBank.exp: Collecting for a company's account cheques drawn payable to another company is conversion. (Module 1, §1.13.8)

questionBank.q: Which of the following best describes the 'policy role' of banks?
opts: A. Banks implement monetary policy through their operations.
B. Banks provide financial advice to governments.
C. Banks act as guarantors for international trade.
questionBank.ans: A. Banks implement monetary policy through their operations.
questionBank.exp: The policy role refers to banks' role in implementing government monetary policy, often through their lending and deposit activities. (Module 1, §1.2.v)

questionBank.q: When a customer enters a banking hall and is greeted by a staff member who directs them to the appropriate service point, this staff member is most likely a:
questionBank.exp: Lobby Service officers welcome and greet customers, direct them to service points, assist with queue management, and answer questions. (Module 2, §2.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Customer Service Unit (CSU)?
opts: C. Processing cash deposits and withdrawals.
D. Receiving and handling customers' complaints.
questionBank.ans: C. Processing cash deposits and withdrawals.
questionBank.exp: Cash deposits and withdrawals are handled by the Cash & Teller Unit. CSU functions include cheque book issuance, signature verification, complaints handling, and standing orders. (Module 2, §2.2)

questionBank.q: A new customer submits a completed account opening form with identification documents. Which of the following is a mandatory document for opening an individual current account?
opts: D. Memorandum and Articles of Association.
questionBank.exp: For an individual current account, required documents include completed forms, identification, utility bill showing address, two passport photographs, two reference forms, and a signature mandate. (Module 2, §2.8.1)

questionBank.q: A customer who holds a current account with a bank requests a cheque book. Before releasing the cheque book, the CSU staff must:
opts: A. Obtain board resolution from the customer.
B. Verify the customer's signature against the mandate.
C. Charge the customer a maintenance fee.
D. Request a new reference form.
questionBank.ans: B. Verify the customer's signature against the mandate.
questionBank.exp: Cheque books are released only as authorised by customers; the bank must verify the customer's identity and signature mandate. (Module 2, §2.4.2.e)

questionBank.q: The Electronic Fund Transfer Levy of N50 is applicable to which of the following transactions?
opts: A. A transfer of ₦5,000 from a customer's savings to current account in the same bank.
B. A transfer of ₦15,000 from a customer's account to a beneficiary in another bank.
C. A cash withdrawal of ₦20,000 over the counter.
D. A cheque payment of ₦10,000 to a third party.
questionBank.ans: B. A transfer of ₦15,000 from a customer's account to a beneficiary in another bank.
questionBank.exp: The EFT Levy imposes N50 on electronic transfers in any financial institution for amounts over ₦10,000. Exemptions include self‑to‑self transfers and withdrawals from savings accounts. (Module 2, §2.12)

questionBank.q: Which of the following accounts does NOT require a Certificate of Incorporation for opening?
questionBank.exp: Partnership accounts require Partnership Agreement, not Certificate of Incorporation. Corporate, Clubs/Associations, and NGOs require registration certificates. (Module 2, §2.8)

questionBank.q: A customer reports that her cheque book has been lost. The bank's immediate response should include:
opts: A. Issuing a new cheque book immediately without delay.
B. Advising the customer to close the account and open a new one.
C. Placing a stop on all unused cheques and monitoring the account.
D. Charging the customer a fee for the lost cheque book.
questionBank.ans: C. Placing a stop on all unused cheques and monitoring the account.
questionBank.exp: Accounts for which cheque books are reported as lost or stolen may be closed and a new account opened; at minimum, stop payment instructions must be noted. (Module 2, §2.14.4)

questionBank.q: What is the primary purpose of the Bank Verification Number (BVN) initiative?
opts: A. To serve as a customer's tax identification number.
B. To provide biometric authentication and identification across all banks.
C. To replace the need for a physical signature on cheques.
D. To calculate the customer's credit score.
questionBank.ans: B. To provide biometric authentication and identification across all banks.
questionBank.exp: The BVN provides biometrics authentication and identification to check identity theft, ensure safety of funds, and increase service levels. (Module 2, §2.13.1)

questionBank.q: A customer wishes to pay his utility bills through a standing order from his current account. The CSU staff should first:
opts: A. Debit the customer's account immediately.
B. Obtain written instructions and log them for treatment.
C. Refer the customer to the bill payment provider.
D. Advise the customer to use the bank's mobile app instead.
questionBank.ans: B. Obtain written instructions and log them for treatment.
questionBank.exp: Standing order procedure: customer issues detailed written instruction; it is received, stamped, and logged; then acknowledgement sent. (Module 2, §2.17.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following documents is typically required for opening a Public Sector account?
opts: A. Certificate of Registration of Business Name.
B. Copy of the Gazette or Decree establishing the institution.
C. Certified copy of Form CAC 2.3.
D. Copy of the Trust Deed.
questionBank.ans: B. Copy of the Gazette or Decree establishing the institution.
questionBank.exp: Public Sector accounts require a copy of Gazette/Decree establishing the institution, letter of authorisation from supervising ministry, and letter appointing signatories. (Module 2, §2.8.5)

questionBank.q: A customer complains that the bank deducted a Current Account Maintenance Fee (CAMF) incorrectly. According to policy, which transaction should NOT attract CAMF?
opts: A. A customer‑induced debit to a current account.
B. A transfer from current account to a savings account in the same name.
C. A returned outward clearing cheque.
D. A cheque payment to a third party.
questionBank.ans: C. A returned outward clearing cheque.
questionBank.exp: Banks should not charge CAMF on returned outward clearing cheques, reversal of transactions, and bank‑induced debits. Transfers to same‑name accounts are also exempt. (Module 2, §2.11.3)

questionBank.q: When a customer calls the bank to stop payment on a cheque, the bank's procedure should be to:
opts: A. Accept the instruction verbally and execute immediately.
B. Advise the customer to put it in writing and only then act.
C. Accept verbally but require written confirmation within a specified time.
D. Refuse verbal instructions as a matter of policy.
questionBank.ans: C. Accept verbally but require written confirmation within a specified time.
questionBank.exp: Stop payment instructions may be accepted over the telephone but must be backed up with written confirmation within a specified time. (Module 2, §2.14.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid reason for deferring documentation during account opening?
opts: A. Statutory documents like Certificate of Incorporation.
B. Non‑regulatory documents for up to 30‑90 days.
D. A customer's promise to bring the documents later.
questionBank.ans: A. Statutory documents like Certificate of Incorporation.
questionBank.exp: Statutory documents such as Certificate of Incorporation or client identification cannot be waived. Deferrals are allowed only for non‑regulatory documents. (Module 2, §2.10.7)

questionBank.q: A new customer, a sole proprietor, wants to open a current account. Which of the following must be provided?
questionBank.exp: For sole proprietorship (individual current account), the requirements include two completed reference forms, identification, utility bill, photographs, and mandate. (Module 2, §2.8.1)

questionBank.q: What is the maximum rate for Current Account Maintenance Fee as per CBN guidelines?
questionBank.exp: The rate is negotiable subject to a maximum of N1 per mille. (Module 2, §2.11.2)

questionBank.q: A customer operates a joint account with her husband. The mandate states 'either to sign'. One of them passes away. The bank should:
opts: A. Continue operations with the surviving signatory only.
B. Freeze the account until a new mandate is received.
C. Require probate before allowing any further transactions.
D. Pay all funds to the deceased's estate immediately.
questionBank.ans: B. Freeze the account until a new mandate is received.
questionBank.exp: When a joint account holder dies, the bank should stop operations and await a new mandate or legal authority (unless the mandate explicitly provides for survivorship). (Module 2, §2.8.2 & §2.14.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a Security Function of the Customer Service Unit?
opts: A. Responding to customers' balance enquiries.
C. Keeping all cheque booklets in fireproof cabinets.
D. Issuing reference letters on behalf of clients.
questionBank.ans: C. Keeping all cheque booklets in fireproof cabinets.
questionBank.exp: Security functions include keeping cheque booklets in fireproof cabinets, complying with SOP on reorder levels, time‑stamping incoming requests, maintaining confidentiality, and releasing cheque books only as authorised. (Module 2, §2.4.2)

questionBank.q: A customer who has been a victim of identity theft reports that someone else has been using his account. The bank should first:
opts: A. Close the account and open a new one.
B. Investigate the incident and involve the BVN system.
D. Advise the customer to change his password.
questionBank.ans: B. Investigate the incident and involve the BVN system.
questionBank.exp: BVN helps check identity theft and ensure safety of funds. The bank should investigate the breach and involve BVN verification. (Module 2, §2.13.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an example of a 'close wrong' distractor in the context of account opening?
opts: A. A customer submits an expired passport as ID.
B. A customer provides a valid driver's license instead of a passport.
C. A customer gives a utility bill in someone else's name.
D. A customer provides a BVN that does not match the name.
questionBank.ans: B. A customer provides a valid driver's license instead of a passport.
questionBank.exp: Close wrong distractors are plausible errors. In this context, a driver's license is a valid ID but may not be accepted if the bank requires a passport specifically – it's a confusing but real alternative. (Module 2, §2.8)

questionBank.q: A customer who has not operated his account for over a year wants to reactivate it. The bank should require:
opts: A. A new account opening form and KYC update.
B. A letter of explanation and a fee.
questionBank.ans: A. A new account opening form and KYC update.
questionBank.exp: Dormant accounts require re‑opening procedures, which include updating customer details and KYC. (Module 2, §2.4.1.g)

questionBank.q: A customer requests that his savings account be converted to a current account. What is the first step for the CSU?
opts: A. Close the savings account and open a new current account.
B. Obtain a new mandate and updated KYC documents.
C. Transfer the balance to the new account without documentation.
D. Charge a conversion fee and proceed.
questionBank.ans: B. Obtain a new mandate and updated KYC documents.
questionBank.exp: When changing account type, the bank must obtain a new mandate and updated customer information, as per account opening procedures. (Module 2, §2.6)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a category of account listed in the manual?
questionBank.exp: Dormant accounts are a status, not a category of account type. Listed categories include Checking, Savings, Minor, Partnership, Investment, Unincorporated, Executor's, External, Domiciliary, and Trustee. (Module 2, §2.6)

questionBank.q: When a customer's signature on a withdrawal instruction does not match the mandate, the bank's correct action is to:
opts: A. Process the transaction and later confirm.
B. Refer the signature to the supervisor for verification.
C. Reject the transaction and notify the customer.
D. Accept it if the customer is known to the bank.
questionBank.ans: C. Reject the transaction and notify the customer.
questionBank.exp: Signature verification is a key function; if it does not match, the instruction should be rejected. (Module 2, §2.2.f)

questionBank.q: The CBN Consumer Protection Framework principle of 'Responsible Business Conduct' requires that financial institutions:
opts: A. Provide financial education to consumers.
B. Assess the financial capabilities of consumers and offer suitable products.
C. Ensure effective enforcement of regulations.
D. Protect consumer assets and privacy.
questionBank.ans: B. Assess the financial capabilities of consumers and offer suitable products.
questionBank.exp: Responsible Business Conduct requires banks to observe high ethical standards, assess financial capabilities, and offer suitable products/services based on needs and capability. (Module 1, §1.14.1.2)

questionBank.q: A bank receives a stop payment instruction from a customer on a cheque already presented for payment. The cheque was paid before the instruction was received. The bank should:
opts: A. Reverse the payment and debit the customer.
B. Advise the customer promptly that the cheque was already paid.
C. Refuse to pay and return the cheque.
D. Ask the clearing house to reverse the transaction.
questionBank.ans: B. Advise the customer promptly that the cheque was already paid.
questionBank.exp: Customers will be advised promptly if a cheque has been paid prior to receipt of stop instruction. (Module 2, §2.14.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a required document for opening a Non‑Governmental Organisation (NGO) account?
opts: C. Certificate of Incorporation of the NGO.
D. Letter of authorization from supervising ministry.
questionBank.exp: NGO account requires Trust Deed, registration certificate, resolution of trustees appointing signatories, and identification of signatories. (Module 2, §2.8.6)

questionBank.q: A customer complains that the bank has been charging him a maintenance fee on his savings account. The bank should inform him that:
opts: A. Savings accounts are not subject to CAMF.
B. Savings accounts are subject to CAMF at the same rate.
C. Only current accounts attract CAMF.
D. The fee is a regulatory requirement.
questionBank.ans: A. Savings accounts are not subject to CAMF.
questionBank.exp: Current Account Maintenance Fee applies to customer‑induced debit transactions on current accounts only. Savings accounts are exempt. (Module 2, §2.11)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a Product and Services Management function of the CSU?
opts: A. Keeping cheque booklets in fireproof cabinets.
C. Knowing and discussing product features with customers.
D. Maintaining confidentiality of customer data.
questionBank.ans: C. Knowing and discussing product features with customers.
questionBank.exp: Product and Services Management includes knowing and discussing product features, knowing account officers, directing customers, and having skills in resolving complaints. (Module 2, §2.4.3.1)

questionBank.q: A customer wants to open a club account. Which document is mandatory in addition to the standard identification?
opts: A. Certificate of Registration of Business Name.
B. Copy of the Constitution of the club.
questionBank.ans: B. Copy of the Constitution of the club.
questionBank.exp: Clubs and Associations require a copy of their constitution, in addition to registration of business name, identification of signatories, reference forms, and photographs. (Module 2, §2.8.4)

questionBank.q: When a customer reports that his cheque book was stolen, the bank should also consider:
opts: A. Closing the account and opening a new one.
B. Issuing a new cheque book immediately.
C. Debiting the customer for all lost cheques.
D. Reporting the theft to the police.
questionBank.ans: A. Closing the account and opening a new one.
questionBank.exp: Accounts for which cheque books are reported as lost or stolen may be closed and a new account opened. (Module 2, §2.14.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following statements about deferrals is correct?
opts: A. Deferrals can be done by any staff member.
B. Deferrals on CO7 should not exceed 30 days.
C. Deferrals on CO7 can be extended indefinitely.
D. Cheque books can be issued even with deferred CO7.
questionBank.ans: B. Deferrals on CO7 should not exceed 30 days.
questionBank.exp: Deferrals on CO7 should not exceed 30 days and no cheque book may be issued. Only very senior executive staff can defer documents for public sector. (Module 2, §2.9)

questionBank.q: A customer calls to complain that he was charged a fee for a transaction that he believes should be free. According to CBN guidelines, which of the following transactions should NOT incur a charge?
opts: A. Transfer from a current account to another bank.
B. Loan repayment from a current account.
C. Cash withdrawal over the counter.
D. Issuance of a bank draft.
questionBank.ans: B. Loan repayment from a current account.
questionBank.exp: No charge on loan repayment from current or savings account. (Module 2, §2.11.5)

questionBank.q: The Customer Service Unit's role in maintaining customer database is part of which functional classification?
questionBank.exp: Client Information Services include maintaining customers' database, handling enquiries, issuing reference letters, and updating BVN. (Module 2, §2.4.1)

questionBank.q: A customer is unable to visit the branch and wants to update his mandate. The bank should:
opts: A. Accept a verbal instruction over the phone.
B. Require the customer to send a written instruction with proper identification.
C. Defer the update until the customer visits.
D. Update the mandate based on the customer's known signature.
questionBank.ans: B. Require the customer to send a written instruction with proper identification.
questionBank.exp: Mandate changes require written instruction and verification. The manual emphasises that all instructions must be written and verified. (Module 2, §2.2.h)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an exception to the Electronic Fund Transfer Levy?
opts: A. Transfers over ₦10,000 between different banks.
B. Withdrawals from a savings account.
C. Payment of utility bills via mobile app.
questionBank.ans: B. Withdrawals from a savings account.
questionBank.exp: Exemptions include payment deposits or transfers by self‑to‑self, any form of withdrawals/transfers from Savings Account, and others. (Module 2, §2.12.1)

questionBank.q: The primary entry point for customers into a bank's services is the:
questionBank.exp: The Cash & Teller Unit is the primary entry into a bank; customers go there for deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. (Module 3, §3.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable feature of the Cash & Teller Unit?
opts: C. Teller tills not being shared.
questionBank.exp: Customers should not wait endlessly; acceptable features include timestamping, separate tills, and vault operations. (Module 3, §3.1.5)

questionBank.q: A teller discovers cash in his cubicle at the beginning of the day that was left overnight. The bank's procedure requires that this cash be:
opts: A. Added to the teller's opening balance.
B. Treated as 'Cash Found on Premises' and handed to the Cash Officer.
C. Kept aside until the customer claims it.
D. Deposited into the teller's personal account.
questionBank.ans: B. Treated as 'Cash Found on Premises' and handed to the Cash Officer.
questionBank.exp: Any cash found in a teller cubicle or cash area should be investigated and treated as 'Cash Found on Premises', handed to the Cash Officer and booked in the GL with approval. (Module 3, §3.6.1)

questionBank.q: The primary purpose of CCTV in the teller area is to:
opts: A. Record customer transactions for audit.
C. Monitor for fraud and deter robberies.
D. Replace the need for a supervisor.
questionBank.ans: C. Monitor for fraud and deter robberies.
questionBank.exp: CCTV helps in teller monitoring for fraud, supervision, deterrence, and customer confidence; it comes useful during investigations. (Module 3, §3.3)

questionBank.q: A bank teller is responsible for all of the following EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: Tellers handle transactions, answer questions, and cross‑sell; they do not approve loans – that is the responsibility of credit officers. (Module 3, §3.4)

questionBank.q: When a teller receives a deposit slip and cash from a customer, the FIRST step is to:
opts: A. Count the cash and agree the estimate.
B. Enter the transaction into the system.
D. Issue a receipt to the customer.
questionBank.ans: A. Count the cash and agree the estimate.
questionBank.exp: The teller receives the deposit slip and cash, and agrees the estimate with the customer before counting. (Module 3, §3.7.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a teller's 'Don't' as listed in the manual?
opts: A. Use mobile phones while attending to customers.
B. Eat or drink in the cubicle in front of customers.
C. Chat with another teller when customers are waiting.
questionBank.exp: Tellers must not eat, drink, shout, frown, use phones, or chat with other tellers while customers are waiting. (Module 3, §3.4.4)

questionBank.q: A customer presents a cheque for cash withdrawal. The teller notices that the amount in words and figures do not agree. The teller should:
opts: A. Pay the amount in words.
B. Pay the amount in figures.
C. Refer the cheque to the supervisor.
D. Return the cheque to the customer.
questionBank.ans: D. Return the cheque to the customer.
questionBank.exp: Cheques with amounts in words and figures that differ are irregular and should be returned to the customer. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: The maximum amount that can be paid to a third‑party payee over the counter is governed by:
opts: A. The bank's own internal policy only.
B. The CBN's cash‑lite policy and regulatory thresholds.
D. The availability of cash in the vault.
questionBank.ans: B. The CBN's cash‑lite policy and regulatory thresholds.
questionBank.exp: Withdrawals on third‑party cheques must comply with cashless banking limits and regulatory thresholds. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: When a teller processes an in‑house account‑to‑account transfer using a cheque, the teller should first:
opts: A. Credit the payee's account immediately.
B. Verify the drawer's signature against the mandate.
C. Debit the drawer's account without verification.
D. Request an approval from the branch manager.
questionBank.ans: B. Verify the drawer's signature against the mandate.
questionBank.exp: For in‑house cheques, the teller must call up the account and verify the drawer's signature against the mandate before passing entries. (Module 3, §3.7.8.b)

questionBank.q: A customer deposits a cheque drawn on another bank into his account. The bank gives value on a T+1 basis. This is because:
opts: A. The cheque must be cleared through the clearing house.
B. The customer requested a delayed value.
C. The bank has a policy of T+2.
questionBank.ans: A. The cheque must be cleared through the clearing house.
questionBank.exp: Other Banks' Cheques (OBC) are deposited with forward value date in line with Bankers' Clearing House Rules (T+1). (Module 3, §3.7.9)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a valid reason for a cash shortage?
opts: C. Cash lodgment exceeding the amount on deposit slip.
D. Mixing personal money with bank funds.
questionBank.exp: Cash shortages can be due to overpayment, posting errors, pilfering, or genuine errors. Underpayment, excess lodgment, and mixing personal money usually cause overages. (Module 3, §3.7.11.1)

questionBank.q: When a teller has a cash difference that cannot be resolved after a call‑over, the next step is to:
opts: A. Ignore the difference and carry it forward.
B. Report to the supervisor and request approval to post to the difference account.
C. Adjust the difference from the teller's personal salary.
D. Cover the difference with the customer's next deposit.
questionBank.ans: B. Report to the supervisor and request approval to post to the difference account.
questionBank.exp: If a difference persists after call‑over, the teller reports to supervisor and requests approval to post the difference to the Teller's specific Cash Difference Account. (Module 3, §3.6.3)

questionBank.q: The primary document used to monitor cash movement between vault and tellers is the:
questionBank.exp: The 'Vault‑In Register' is used for monitoring movement in and out of the vault. (Module 3, §3.6.1)

questionBank.q: Under the Subject to Count (STC) agreement, if a shortage is discovered after detail counting, the bank should:
opts: B. Debit the customer's account and advise them.
C. Refuse to accept future STC deposits.
D. Report the matter to the police.
questionBank.ans: B. Debit the customer's account and advise them.
questionBank.exp: In STC, if a shortage is discovered, the bank debits the customer's account under advice. (Module 3, §3.7.7)

questionBank.q: A teller's proof sheet is used to:
opts: B. Show the summary of activities at the teller point in a day.
questionBank.ans: B. Show the summary of activities at the teller point in a day.
questionBank.exp: The proof sheet shows the summary of activities, including till balance, cash paid/received, and records of shortages/overages. (Module 3, §3.9)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a control measure for tellers?
opts: A. Sharing passwords with colleagues for backup.
B. Balancing cash every 2 to 3 hours.
C. Leaving cash drawers unlocked during breaks.
D. Using a colleague's till for customer transactions.
questionBank.ans: B. Balancing cash every 2 to 3 hours.
questionBank.exp: Controls include balancing cash every 2‑3 hours, locking PCs and drawers, protecting passwords, and reviewing transactions. (Module 3, §3.10.2)

questionBank.q: A customer deposits a foreign currency (FCY) cash. The teller must first:
opts: A. Convert the amount at the bank's buying rate.
B. Verify the cash using a testing machine or currency tester.
C. Credit the customer's domiciliary account immediately.
D. Enter the transaction into the system.
questionBank.ans: B. Verify the cash using a testing machine or currency tester.
questionBank.exp: FCY cash deposits require verification using a testing machine or currency tester to ensure genuineness before processing entries. (Module 3, §3.7.2.5)

questionBank.q: The vault custodian and the Head of Operations jointly lock the vault at the end of the day using:
opts: C. Both dual keys and combination numbers.
questionBank.ans: C. Both dual keys and combination numbers.
questionBank.exp: Vault Custodian and Head of Operations lock the vault using dual control keys and combination numbers. (Module 3, §3.6.3)

questionBank.q: A teller receives a late cash deposit after the system cut‑off time. The correct procedure is to:
opts: A. Credit the customer's account immediately.
B. Deposit the cash and credit the account the next business day.
C. Return the cash to the customer.
D. Hold the cash and issue a temporary receipt.
questionBank.ans: B. Deposit the cash and credit the account the next business day.
questionBank.exp: Late deposits are verified and counted, but entries are not passed until the next business day; a 'late deposit for credit on (date)' stamp is applied. (Module 3, §3.7.6)

questionBank.q: A customer withdraws cash from his domiciliary account in US dollars. The teller charges a commission of 1% and VAT of 7.5% on the commission. The VAT is calculated on:
questionBank.exp: VAT of 7.5% is charged on the commission (1% of the transaction amount), not on the principal withdrawal. (Module 3, §3.7.5)

questionBank.q: A teller counts the cash in her till and finds that the physical cash exceeds the system balance. This situation is called:
questionBank.exp: A cash overage occurs when physical cash is more than the system balance. (Module 3, §3.7.11.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a source of cash deposits into the vault?
opts: A. Cash deposited into customers' accounts.
B. Cash sweep from customer collection points.
D. Proceeds from online banking transfers.
questionBank.ans: D. Proceeds from online banking transfers.
questionBank.exp: Sources of cash deposits include customer account deposits, local collection, cash sweep, CBN withdrawals, and proceeds from asset disposal. Online transfers are not cash deposits. (Module 3, §3.8.6)

questionBank.q: A teller processes a cash withdrawal for a customer who has an incomplete mandate. The teller should:
opts: A. Process the withdrawal if the customer is known.
B. Request additional approval from the supervisor.
C. Deny the withdrawal until the mandate is completed.
D. Ask the customer to fill a new withdrawal slip.
questionBank.ans: C. Deny the withdrawal until the mandate is completed.
questionBank.exp: Withdrawals on accounts with incomplete documentation require additional approvals or may be denied; in principle, the mandate must be complete. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: When evacuating excess cash from tellers to the vault, which document is completed and signed by both parties?
questionBank.exp: Teller transfer slips are completed in duplicate and signed off by teller and vault custodian for any cash movement into/out of the vault. (Module 3, §3.6.1)

questionBank.q: A customer deposits cash into a savings account but the deposit slip has the wrong account number. The teller should:
opts: A. Credit the account number on the slip.
B. Ask the customer to confirm the correct number and correct the slip.
D. Credit the customer's other account.
questionBank.ans: B. Ask the customer to confirm the correct number and correct the slip.
questionBank.exp: The teller must review the deposit slip for regularity; if the account number is wrong, the customer should confirm and correct it before processing. (Module 3, §3.7.1)

questionBank.q: The Head Teller combines all teller proofs onto a departmental proof for the purpose of:
opts: B. Reconciling the general ledger cash account.
questionBank.ans: B. Reconciling the general ledger cash account.
questionBank.exp: The Head Teller combines proofs and verifies inter‑departmental postings to reconcile the GL cash account. (Module 3, §3.9.8.b)

questionBank.q: A teller discovers that a counterfeit note was accepted earlier in the day. The immediate action should be:
opts: B. Notify the supervisor and follow the bank's counterfeit procedure.
C. Re‑issue the note to another customer.
questionBank.ans: B. Notify the supervisor and follow the bank's counterfeit procedure.
questionBank.exp: The manual notes that tellers check for counterfeits under ultraviolet light; if discovered, the bank's policy on counterfeit handling must be followed, which includes reporting. (Module 3, §3.7.1)

questionBank.q: A customer requests a cash advance for staff expenses. The teller processes it by:
opts: A. Debiting the customer's account and crediting cash.
B. Debiting the bank's operating expense account.
questionBank.ans: A. Debiting the customer's account and crediting cash.
questionBank.exp: Cash advances (IOUs) are treated as normal cash withdrawals; the customer's account is debited and cash is credited. (Module 3, §3.7.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a Bulk Teller?
opts: B. Handles large volume of cash and cheque deposits from corporate customers.
C. Works only with foreign currency.
questionBank.ans: B. Handles large volume of cash and cheque deposits from corporate customers.
questionBank.exp: Bulk Tellers handle large volume cash deposits and withdrawals, often for corporate customers; they are part of the teller team. (Module 3, §3.5)

questionBank.q: The dual custody requirement for vault compartments means that:
opts: A. Two people must be present to open the vault.
B. One person has the key and the other has the combination.
C. The vault custodian and the teller both unlock their respective compartments.
D. The branch manager and cash officer are both required.
questionBank.ans: C. The vault custodian and the teller both unlock their respective compartments.
questionBank.exp: Each custodian unlocks combination for their own side; tellers remove their numbered cashboxes and sign out; cash officer initials. (Module 3, §3.8.3)

questionBank.q: A teller notices that a customer's withdrawal cheque is stale‑dated (more than 6 months old). The correct action is to:
opts: A. Pay the cheque if funds are available.
B. Return the cheque as stale.
C. Request a new cheque from the customer.
D. Hold the cheque and wait for clearance.
questionBank.ans: B. Return the cheque as stale.
questionBank.exp: Stale‑dated cheques are irregular and must be returned. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: When a teller processes a cash withdrawal for a third‑party payee, what identification is required?
opts: A. No identification if the cheque is crossed.
B. Acceptable means of identification (e.g., passport, driver's license).
questionBank.ans: B. Acceptable means of identification (e.g., passport, driver's license).
questionBank.exp: For third‑party payees, obtain acceptable means of identification in line with policy. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: A teller receives a withdrawal slip for a savings account that would cause the account to go into debit. The teller should:
opts: A. Process the withdrawal if there is an overdraft arrangement.
B. Reject the withdrawal because savings accounts cannot be thrown into debit.
C. Request approval from the branch manager.
D. Convert the account to a current account.
questionBank.ans: B. Reject the withdrawal because savings accounts cannot be thrown into debit.
questionBank.exp: Savings accounts cannot be thrown into debit; withdrawals must not exceed the available balance. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a key control to prevent cash handling fraud?
opts: A. Allowing tellers to share passwords.
B. Leaving cash drawers open for easy access.
C. Ensuring all registers are completed and reviewed daily by supervisors.
D. Allowing tellers to self‑approve their own transactions.
questionBank.ans: C. Ensuring all registers are completed and reviewed daily by supervisors.
questionBank.exp: Key controls include completing and reviewing registers daily, locking PCs/drawers, not sharing passwords, and escalating irregularities. (Module 3, §3.10.2)

questionBank.q: A customer deposits a cheque into his account, and the cheque is later returned by the drawee bank. The bank should:
opts: A. Debit the customer's account and advise him.
C. Present the cheque again without notifying the customer.
D. Contact the drawer's bank directly.
questionBank.ans: A. Debit the customer's account and advise him.
questionBank.exp: Returned cheques must be reversed by debiting the customer's account; this is a standard procedure. (Module 3, §3.7.9)

questionBank.q: According to the cash packaging table, one bundle of ₦200 notes contains how many individual pieces?
questionBank.exp: One pack has 100 pieces, and one bundle has 5 packs, so 5 × 100 = 500 pieces. (Module 3, §3.7.10)

questionBank.q: A teller receives a deposit slip and cash, but the total amount written on the slip is higher than the cash counted. The teller should:
opts: A. Credit the amount on the slip and note the shortage.
B. Inform the customer of the discrepancy and correct the slip.
C. Accept the cash and ignore the slip.
D. Deposit the cash and later adjust.
questionBank.ans: B. Inform the customer of the discrepancy and correct the slip.
questionBank.exp: If the counted cash does not agree with the deposit slip, the teller should notify the customer of the discrepancy and correct the slip. (Module 3, §3.7.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a function of the Cash & Teller Unit?
opts: B. Handling government collections like customs duties.
D. Managing the bank's investment portfolio.
questionBank.ans: B. Handling government collections like customs duties.
questionBank.exp: CTU functions include government collections, handling deposits/withdrawals, processing cheques, cash pick‑ups, and fraud prevention. (Module 3, §3.5)

questionBank.q: The time‑stamping machine slug (validating key) is stored in the teller's till box at the end of the day to:
opts: A. Prevent unauthorised use of the time stamp.
B. Keep the machine ready for the next day.
C. Record the date of the next business day.
D. Ensure the time is set correctly.
questionBank.ans: A. Prevent unauthorised use of the time stamp.
questionBank.exp: The slug (validating key) is removed from the till box and stored securely to prevent unauthorised use of the time‑stamping machine. (Module 3, §3.6.1)

questionBank.q: A customer wants to withdraw cash from his current account using a withdrawal slip. The teller must first:
opts: A. Check the customer's account balance.
C. Count the cash to be dispensed.
D. Enter the transaction into the system.
questionBank.exp: Signature verification is the first step for any withdrawal, to ensure the instruction is authorised. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: A teller processes a cash deposit and later discovers that the deposit slip was not signed. The correct action is:
opts: B. Contact the customer to obtain a signature.
D. Note the omission and continue.
questionBank.ans: B. Contact the customer to obtain a signature.
questionBank.exp: All deposit slips must be properly completed; if not signed, the teller should obtain the customer's signature. (Module 3, §3.7.1)

questionBank.q: The maximum cash holding limit for a teller's cubicle is determined by:
opts: B. The bank's internal policy and regulatory guidelines.
questionBank.ans: B. The bank's internal policy and regulatory guidelines.
questionBank.exp: Tellers must comply with teller cash holding limits, which are set by bank policy and regulatory requirements. (Module 3, §3.1.5)

questionBank.q: A teller receives a cheque that has been altered (amount changed). The alteration is not countersigned by the drawer. The teller should:
opts: A. Accept the cheque and process it.
B. Return the cheque to the customer.
C. Request the drawer's confirmation before paying.
questionBank.ans: B. Return the cheque to the customer.
questionBank.exp: Material alterations must be signed by the drawer; otherwise, the cheque is irregular. (Module 3, §3.7.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a key skill for a bank teller?
opts: A. Advanced knowledge of international trade.
questionBank.exp: Teller skills include communication, numeric, interpersonal, listening, problem‑solving, product knowledge, discerning, and speed. (Module 3, §3.4.2)

questionBank.q: A customer withdraws cash from his account and the teller accidentally gives him ₦5,000 more than requested. The teller should:
opts: A. Hide the error and hope the customer doesn't notice.
B. Report the overpayment immediately and attempt to recover the excess.
C. Deduct the amount from the teller's salary.
D. Wait for the customer to return.
questionBank.ans: B. Report the overpayment immediately and attempt to recover the excess.
questionBank.exp: Cash overages (under‑payment) or shortages (over‑payment) must be reported and corrected; the teller must follow the difference procedure. (Module 3, §3.7.11)

questionBank.q: The 'cashing‑in' procedure refers to:
opts: A. Moving cash from vault to teller.
B. Moving cash from teller to vault.
C. Depositing cash into a customer's account.
D. Withdrawing cash from the customer's account.
questionBank.ans: A. Moving cash from vault to teller.
questionBank.exp: Cashing‑in is the procedure of posting cash allocation from the vault to the teller's position. (Module 3, §3.6.1)

questionBank.q: A teller receives a cash deposit from a customer who is not an account holder. The teller should:
opts: A. Accept the deposit and credit a suspense account.
B. Reject the deposit because only account holders can deposit cash.
C. Accept the deposit and ask the customer to open an account later.
D. Confirm the customer's identity and accept the deposit.
questionBank.ans: B. Reject the deposit because only account holders can deposit cash.
questionBank.exp: Cash deposits are accepted only for accounts; a non‑account holder cannot deposit cash into someone else's account without proper authorisation. (Module 3, §3.7.1)

questionBank.q: The primary purpose of the departmental proof is to:
opts: B. Aggregate teller proofs for reconciliation.
questionBank.ans: B. Aggregate teller proofs for reconciliation.
questionBank.exp: The Head Teller combines all teller proofs onto a departmental proof to reconcile the GL cash account. (Module 3, §3.9.8)

questionBank.q: A customer deposits cash subject to count (STC). The agreement allows the bank to:
opts: A. Count the cash immediately and credit.
B. Credit the account immediately and later adjust.
C. Hold the cash for 5 days before counting.
D. Charge the customer a counting fee.
questionBank.ans: B. Credit the account immediately and later adjust.
questionBank.exp: In STC, the bank passes entries immediately and counts in detail within 24 hours, then adjusts for any surplus or shortage. (Module 3, §3.7.7)

questionBank.q: The Nigerian Bankers' Clearing House (NBCH) was established under which legislation?
opts: B. Section 47 of the CBN Act No. 7 of 2007.
C. The Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act 2020.
D. The Nigerian Interbank Settlement Systems Act.
questionBank.ans: B. Section 47 of the CBN Act No. 7 of 2007.
questionBank.exp: S.47 of CBN Act No. 7 of 2007 set up the Nigerian Bankers' Clearing House (NBCH). (Module 4, §4.1.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Nigerian Bankers' Clearing House?
questionBank.exp: Member Banks include CBN, DMBs (settlement/non-settlement), and NIBSS. Fintechs are not members. (Module 4, §4.1.4)

questionBank.q: The minimum clearing collateral required for a non‑settlement bank is currently:
questionBank.exp: Clearing collateral by Non-Settlement Banks is N250 million while that of Settlement Banks is N15 Billion. (Module 4, §4.3.9)

questionBank.q: The new Nigeria Cheque Standard became fully operational on which date?
questionBank.exp: The new Nigeria Cheque Standard became fully operational on April 1, 2021, with parallel run starting in September 2019. (Module 4, §4.5)

questionBank.q: Under the cheque truncation system, the original physical cheque is stored by which party?
opts: D. The Central Bank of Nigeria.
questionBank.exp: Under truncation, original cheques are stored by the collecting bank. (Module 4, §4.10.2.8)

questionBank.q: A bank that persistently overdraws its settlement account maintained with CBN may face which consequence?
opts: A. A fine of ₦1,000 per item.
C. A warning letter from CBN.
D. A reduction in clearing collateral.
questionBank.exp: If a Bank persistently overdraws its Settlement Account maintained with CBN, it may be suspended. (Module 4, §4.1.8.b)

questionBank.q: A Special Caution Notice must be submitted by the paying bank within what timeframe after the closure of the return cheque session?
questionBank.exp: The deadline for submission of Special Caution Notice is two (2) hours after the closure of return cheque session. (Module 4, §4.6)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an approved reason for returning a clearing instrument?
opts: B. Cheque amount is too large.
C. The payee requested a different currency.
D. The cheque is not signed by the payee.
questionBank.exp: Approved reasons include mutilated cheques, stale/post‑dated, irregular endorsement, account closed, etc. (Module 4, §4.7)

questionBank.q: Under the cheque truncation process, clearing demarcation is:
questionBank.exp: Under cheque truncation, clearing demarcation is T+1. (Module 4, §4.10.2.5)

questionBank.q: The penalty for issuing a dishonoured cheque for an individual under the Dud Cheques Act is:
opts: A. A fine of N5,000 only.
B. Imprisonment for two years without option of fine.
C. Imprisonment for one year or a fine.
questionBank.ans: B. Imprisonment for two years without option of fine.
questionBank.exp: The penalty for an individual is imprisonment for two years without option of fine; for corporate bodies, a fine of not less than N5,000. (Module 4, §4.12.1)

questionBank.q: A presenting bank fails to honour a duly served Special Caution Notice. Under the clearing rules, the presenting bank shall be:
opts: A. Fully liable for the loss.
D. Liable only for administrative fees.
questionBank.ans: A. Fully liable for the loss.
questionBank.exp: Presenting Bank shall be fully liable for the loss where it fails to honour Special Caution Notice. (Module 4, §4.6)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an abuse of the clearing process?
opts: A. Issuing a manager's cheque on a funded account.
B. Drawing instruments on unfunded accounts.
C. Presenting cheques within the clearing window.
D. Returning a forged instrument to the presenting bank.
questionBank.ans: B. Drawing instruments on unfunded accounts.
questionBank.exp: Abuses include drawing instruments on unfunded accounts, persistent presentation of forged instruments, and charging beneficiaries for inward ACH credits. (Module 4, §4.8)

questionBank.q: Under the cheque truncation system, there are how many clearing sessions in a day?
questionBank.exp: The Clearing System operates 4 sessions: 8am, 11am, 2pm, and 5pm. (Module 4, §4.10.2.10)

questionBank.q: A cheque that is presented for clearing three times without payment should be returned with which reason code?
questionBank.exp: Reason code 23 is 'Presented more than 3 times'. (Module 4, §4.7 table)

questionBank.q: The maximum cheque value that can be processed through the clearing system as initially fixed by CBN is:
questionBank.exp: The initial limit fixed by the CBN is N10 million; it can change later. (Module 4, §4.10.2.4)

questionBank.q: A bank receives an inward clearing cheque that is not funded. The bank returns it with reason code 'Account not funded'. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Inward returned cheques are those drawn on your bank and returned for reasons such as insufficient funds. (Module 4, §4.9)

questionBank.q: Under the new Nigeria Cheque Standard, which feature is required on all cheques?
opts: A. A signature panel on the front.
B. MICR characters for automated processing.
C. A photograph of the account holder.
D. A barcode for digital tracking.
questionBank.ans: B. MICR characters for automated processing.
questionBank.exp: The new standard includes MICR encoding for automated clearing; the design is shown in the manual. (Module 4, §4.5)

questionBank.q: A paying bank that fails to return an unpaid instrument within the clearing window shall be:
opts: A. Fully liable for the amount.
B. Liable for a penalty of ₦1,000 per item.
C. Liable jointly with the presenting bank.
questionBank.ans: A. Fully liable for the amount.
questionBank.exp: Failure to return unpaid instrument within the clearing window: paying bank shall be liable. (Module 4, §4.13 table)

questionBank.q: A cheque that is drawn in a foreign currency must be:
opts: A. Treated as invalid and rejected.
C. Converted to naira at the clearing house.
D. Returned with reason 'Bank not in clearing'.
questionBank.exp: Reason code 9: 'Cheque drawn in foreign currency. Please present specially.' (Module 4, §4.7 table)

questionBank.q: The Nigerian Uniform Bank Account Number (NUBAN) was introduced as part of which initiative?
opts: D. The Bank Verification Number (BVN) system.
questionBank.exp: The PSV2020 initiative led to updating the Clearing House Rules and commencement of NUBAN. (Module 4, §4.10.1.6)

questionBank.q: A bank's failure to provide acceptable or competent representatives to the clearing house may result in:
questionBank.exp: Reasons for suspension include failure to provide acceptable or competent representatives. (Module 4, §4.1.8.d)

questionBank.q: Under the cheque truncation process, what is the role of the presenting bank regarding the physical cheque?
opts: A. It must send the physical cheque to the paying bank.
B. It must store the physical cheque securely.
C. It must destroy the physical cheque after scanning.
D. It must return the physical cheque to the customer.
questionBank.ans: B. It must store the physical cheque securely.
questionBank.exp: The collecting (presenting) bank stores the original cheques under the truncation process. (Module 4, §4.10.2.8)

questionBank.q: A customer deposits a cheque drawn on another bank. Under the clearing rules, the customer receives value at what time on T+1?
opts: A. At the start of business.
questionBank.exp: The Revised Nigeria Bankers' Clearing System Rules 2018 states that customers shall receive value in the evening of T+1 by 10pm. (Module 4, §4.10.2.9.b)

questionBank.q: Which of the following instruments is eligible for clearing?
questionBank.exp: Eligible instruments include cheques, drafts, dividend warrants, interest warrants, debit/credit notes, bankers' payments, direct debits, and electronic ACH items. (Module 4, §4.2.1)

questionBank.q: A bank that presents a cheque with an irregularity leading to fraud will be held:
opts: B. Jointly liable with the paying bank (50:50).
D. Liable for administrative penalties only.
questionBank.ans: B. Jointly liable with the paying bank (50:50).
questionBank.exp: Clearing of cheques with irregularity leading to fraud: presenting and paying bank shall be jointly liable (50:50). (Module 4, §4.13 table)

questionBank.q: The CBN can impose a sanction of ₦1,000 per item for which of the following?
opts: B. Presenting non‑NUBAN transactions for clearing.
C. Failure to honour a special caution notice.
questionBank.ans: B. Presenting non‑NUBAN transactions for clearing.
questionBank.exp: Presenting non‑NUBAN transactions for clearing: ₦1,000 per transaction. (Module 4, §4.13 table)

questionBank.q: The 2pm clearing session permits which type of instruments?
opts: B. Returned cheques, fresh NEFT DR/CR, and returned NEFT DR/CR.
questionBank.ans: B. Returned cheques, fresh NEFT DR/CR, and returned NEFT DR/CR.
questionBank.exp: The 2pm session permits only returned cheques, fresh NEFT DR/CR, and returned NEFT DR/CR. Fresh cheques are not allowed. (Module 4, §4.10.2.10 table)

questionBank.q: When a cheque is returned with reason 'Endorsement irregular', what is the most likely cause?
opts: A. The cheque is not signed.
B. The payee's endorsement is not in accordance with the bank's requirements.
questionBank.ans: B. The payee's endorsement is not in accordance with the bank's requirements.
questionBank.exp: Reason 16: 'Endorsement irregular' – the endorsement on the cheque does not meet the required standards. (Module 4, §4.7 table)

questionBank.q: A serial issuer of dud cheques will be barred from the clearing system for a period of:
questionBank.exp: Banks are required to bar affected customers from use of the clearing system for 5 years. (Module 4, §4.12.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the cheque truncation process?
opts: A. Conversion of physical cheque to electronic form.
B. Transmission of scanned image to paying bank.
C. Retention of original cheque by paying bank.
D. Elimination of physical cheque exchange.
questionBank.ans: C. Retention of original cheque by paying bank.
questionBank.exp: The original cheque is retained by the collecting bank, not the paying bank. (Module 4, §4.10.2)

questionBank.q: A bank that charges beneficiaries for inward ACH credits is committing which type of abuse?
opts: B. Charging beneficiaries for inward ACH credits.
C. Delayed presentation of ACH items.
D. Drawing instruments on unfunded accounts.
questionBank.ans: B. Charging beneficiaries for inward ACH credits.
questionBank.exp: Abuses include charging beneficiaries for inward ACH credits. (Module 4, §4.8.4)

questionBank.q: The first clearing session of the day (8am) processes which instruments?
opts: A. Fresh cheques, Fresh NEFT DR/CR, Returned NEFT CR.
questionBank.ans: A. Fresh cheques, Fresh NEFT DR/CR, Returned NEFT CR.
questionBank.exp: The 8am session processes fresh cheques, fresh NEFT DR/CR, returned NEFT CR. (Module 4, §4.10.2.10 table)

questionBank.q: A paying bank that pays a duplicated cheque is liable for the full amount, as per clearing sanctions. This is because:
opts: A. The bank failed to verify the cheque number.
B. The bank should have stopped payment.
C. The bank had already paid the original cheque.
D. The bank is always liable for duplicate payment.
questionBank.ans: C. The bank had already paid the original cheque.
questionBank.exp: Payment of duplicated cheques: paying bank shall be fully liable. (Module 4, §4.13 table)

questionBank.q: Under the CBN measures to dissuade dud cheques, banks are required to perform a status check on potential customers from:
opts: B. CRMS and at least two Credit Bureau.
questionBank.ans: B. CRMS and at least two Credit Bureau.
questionBank.exp: Banks must perform status checks on potential customers from CRMS and at least two Credit Bureau before onboarding. (Module 4, §4.12.3)

questionBank.q: A bank refuses to pay its own Manager's Cheque. According to the clearing rules, this is considered an abuse because:
opts: A. Manager's cheques are not negotiable.
B. A bank should not refuse to pay its own instrument.
C. Manager's cheques are only valid for 30 days.
D. The bank must pay all cheques without question.
questionBank.ans: B. A bank should not refuse to pay its own instrument.
questionBank.exp: Abuses include a Bank refusing to pay its own instrument drawn on itself (Manager's Cheque / Draft). (Module 4, §4.8.6)

questionBank.q: The deadline for acknowledgement of a Special Caution Notice by the presenting bank is:
questionBank.exp: Special Caution Notice shall be acknowledged by the Presenting Bank to be binding; if not returned same working day, it is deemed honoured. (Module 4, §4.6)

questionBank.q: A cheque that has been paid and later presented again will be returned with which reason code?
questionBank.exp: Reason 22: 'Cheque Already Paid' is used when a cheque is presented more than once after payment. (Module 4, §4.7 table)

questionBank.q: A bank that fails to report a serial issuer of dud cheques to CBN CRMS shall be:
questionBank.exp: Any bank that fails to report to CBN CRMS shall be sanctioned accordingly. (Module 4, §4.12.3)

questionBank.q: The 5pm clearing session permits which instruments?
opts: A. Fresh cheques and fresh NEFT debits.
B. Returned cheques, returned NEFT, and fresh NEFT CR.
C. All instruments including fresh cheques.
questionBank.ans: B. Returned cheques, returned NEFT, and fresh NEFT CR.
questionBank.exp: The 5pm session permits returned cheques, returned NEFT DR/CR instruments, and fresh NEFT CR allowed (no fresh cheques, no NEFT debit because NEFT debit must be returned same day). (Module 4, §4.10.2.10 table)

questionBank.q: A bank that persistently fails to maintain adequate clearing collateral may face:
opts: D. An increase in collateral requirement.
questionBank.exp: Failure to maintain adequate clearing collateral is a ground for suspension. (Module 4, §4.1.8.e)

questionBank.q: The unit where treasury transactions are processed is referred to as:
questionBank.exp: Treasury operations (TROPS) refer to the unit where treasury transactions are processed (Money Market and other Treasury transactions). (Module 5, §5.1.1)

questionBank.q: TROPS is responsible for all of the following functions EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: TROPS processes trades but does not initiate them; initiation is done by the front office/treasury dealers. (Module 5, §5.2)

questionBank.q: A bank that has no branch in a location can appoint another bank to provide services to its customers. This arrangement is known as:
questionBank.exp: A bank that has no branch in a location can appoint a correspondent bank; such interaction between two local banks is known as DCBS. (Module 5, §5.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a treasury product offered to customers?
questionBank.exp: Treasury products for customers include Fixed, Call and Term deposits, Domiciliary deposits, and Investment Products. (Module 5, §5.5.1)

questionBank.q: The minimum purchase sum for Treasury Bills as per CBN current guideline is:
questionBank.exp: Banks can pool funds from individuals to make up the minimum purchase sum of ₦50m for Treasury Bills. (Module 5, §5.5.2.2)

questionBank.q: Which money market instrument is NOT secured unless a bank adds its guarantee?
questionBank.exp: Commercial Papers are not secured except a bank adds its guarantee, making it a Guaranteed Commercial Paper (GCP). (Module 5, §5.5.3.2)

questionBank.q: For Bankers Acceptances (BA), the primary obligor is the:
questionBank.exp: The Bank is the primary obligor for BA so the value will be recorded on the balance sheet. (Module 5, §5.5.3.5)

questionBank.q: The aggregate value of Commercial Papers and Bankers Acceptances must not exceed what percentage of a bank's equity capital?
questionBank.exp: The CBN rule is that both BA and CP must not exceed 150% of the equity capital of a bank. (Module 5, §5.5.3.4)

questionBank.q: A customer instructs the bank to purchase foreign exchange for an eligible transaction. The source document for this transaction is a:
questionBank.exp: Foreign Exchange Deal Slips from the Foreign Exchange Department contain details such as date, amount, name of dealers, and settlement dates. (Module 5, §5.6.1.2.e)

questionBank.q: The RTGS system used for transferring large funds between banks in Nigeria now runs on which platform?
questionBank.exp: RTGS has been running on SWIFT since September 4, 2014. (Module 5, §5.6.2.2 & §5.7.3.c)

questionBank.q: Which processing platform is used for foreign currency transactions and settlements between correspondent banks?
questionBank.exp: SWIFT is used for processing foreign currency transactions and settlements between correspondent banks. (Module 5, §5.7.3.d)

questionBank.q: When a TROPS officer receives a deal slip, the first verification step is to:
opts: B. Confirm that the deal slip is time‑stamped and signed by two dealers.
C. Transfer funds to the counter party.
questionBank.ans: B. Confirm that the deal slip is time‑stamped and signed by two dealers.
questionBank.exp: TROPS officer vets the deal slip to ensure it is time‑stamped and signed by two dealers. (Module 5, §5.8)

questionBank.q: A bank receives a deal slip but the counter party has exceeded its approved placement line. The TROPS officer should:
opts: A. Process the transaction and seek approval later.
B. Return the deal slip to the dealer.
C. Approve the transaction without changes.
D. Reduce the amount to fit the line.
questionBank.ans: B. Return the deal slip to the dealer.
questionBank.exp: If the counter party does not have a placement line or has exceeded the approved line, the TROPS officer will return the deal slip to the dealer. (Module 5, §5.8)

questionBank.q: An Open Buy Back (OBB) transaction is secured by:
questionBank.exp: Open Buy Back and Fixed Buy Back are inter‑bank placements secured by Treasury Bills. (Module 5, §5.11.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is TRUE about Open Buy Back (OBB) transactions?
opts: A. They are fixed for a specific period and cannot be called early.
B. They can be as short as 1 day (overnight) or as long as 91 days.
C. They are unsecured inter‑bank placements.
D. They must have a fixed maturity date.
questionBank.ans: B. They can be as short as 1 day (overnight) or as long as 91 days.
questionBank.exp: OBB has flexible timing – can be as short as 1 day (overnight) or as long as 91 days. (Module 5, §5.11.3.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a key internal control tool in TROPS?
opts: A. Delegation of all duties to one officer.
B. Segregation of duties between initiation, confirmation, recording, and settlement.
D. Sharing passwords among team members.
questionBank.ans: B. Segregation of duties between initiation, confirmation, recording, and settlement.
questionBank.exp: Segregation of duties ensures one person is not allowed to initiate and conclude a transaction. (Module 5, §5.10.1)

questionBank.q: TROPS staff should never implement verbal instructions because:
opts: A. Verbal instructions are not efficient.
B. Verbal instructions can be denied.
C. Verbal instructions are not recorded.
D. Management does not give verbal instructions.
questionBank.ans: B. Verbal instructions can be denied.
questionBank.exp: Members of staff should not implement verbal instruction – even from top Management – because verbal instruction can be denied. (Module 5, §5.10.5)

questionBank.q: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) is maintained by which institution?
opts: A. The Federal Ministry of Finance.
B. The Central Bank of Nigeria.
questionBank.ans: B. The Central Bank of Nigeria.
questionBank.exp: The Central Bank of Nigeria maintains the Consolidated Account for TSA. (Module 5, §5.13.3.1)

questionBank.q: Under the Treasury Single Account (TSA), accounts of MDAs with commercial banks must be zeroized:
opts: C. At the end of each banking day.
questionBank.ans: C. At the end of each banking day.
questionBank.exp: The Accounts of the MDAs with Commercial banks must be zeroized at the end of every banking day. (Module 5, §5.13.3.4)

questionBank.q: A TROPS officer receives a CBN statement showing a debit for Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR). This is an example of:
opts: B. A direct debit from CBN.
questionBank.ans: B. A direct debit from CBN.
questionBank.exp: TROPS is responsible for raising entries for CBN direct debits and credits, including CRR. (Module 5, §5.3.1.b)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a foreign currency treasury product?
questionBank.exp: Foreign currency products include sales to BDC, sales to customers for eligible transactions, interbank FX trades (spots, forwards, SWAPS), and foreign exchange transfers. (Module 5, §5.5.4)

questionBank.q: A bank sells Treasury Bills in the secondary market. The TROPS officer must process this as:
opts: B. A local currency treasury transaction.
questionBank.ans: B. A local currency treasury transaction.
questionBank.exp: Treasury Bills – primary and secondary markets sales, purchases, and trading – are local currency investment products. (Module 5, §5.5.2.1.a)

questionBank.q: In TROPS, the department that executes transactions for cash investment, funding, and foreign exchange is the:
questionBank.exp: Treasury Department functionally executes transactions for cash investment, funding, foreign exchange, and risk hedging. (Module 5, §5.1.5)

questionBank.q: For a TROPS transaction, the staff who prepares the source document should not be the one to:
opts: C. Approve or authorize its posting.
questionBank.ans: C. Approve or authorize its posting.
questionBank.exp: The staff that prepares the source document should not be the one to approve or authorize its posting. (Module 5, §5.10.2)

questionBank.q: A bank's TROPS unit receives a deal slip for a Fixed Buy Back (FBB) transaction. What distinguishes FBB from OBB?
opts: B. FBB has a fixed period and cannot be called early.
C. FBB is for foreign currency only.
D. FBB has no maturity date.
questionBank.ans: B. FBB has a fixed period and cannot be called early.
