questionBank.exp: FBB, being a fixed buy back, the counterparty or the bank cannot call for its deposit any time. OBB can be called any time. (Module 5, §5.11.3.6)

questionBank.q: The CBN interbank Funds Transfer Settlement System (CIFTS) is now known as:
questionBank.exp: CBN Interbank Funds Transfer (CIFT) has been renamed the Nigeria Settlement System (NISS). (Module 5, §5.6.2.1 & §6.9)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a TROPS processing platform?
questionBank.exp: NIP is a product of NIBSS, not a TROPS processing platform. Platforms include Core Banking Packages, RTGS, NISS, CIFT, SWIFT, Bloomberg, and Calypso. (Module 5, §5.7.3)

questionBank.q: A TROPS officer must ensure compliance with the department's authorization limits. These limits are designed to:
opts: A. Restrict staff from processing transactions.
B. Ensure only senior staff can approve large amounts.
C. Prevent fraud and ensure proper oversight.
questionBank.ans: C. Prevent fraud and ensure proper oversight.
questionBank.exp: Authorization limits – setting limits for staff – prevent fraud and ensure segregation of duties; routine checks ensure compliance. (Module 5, §5.10.3)

questionBank.q: Under the TSA, commercial banks act as collection agents for government revenue. They are required to:
opts: A. Retain the revenue for operational expenses.
B. Remit all monies to the CBN Consolidated Account at the end of each banking day.
C. Invest the revenue in Treasury Bills.
D. Transfer the revenue to the Ministry of Finance monthly.
questionBank.ans: B. Remit all monies to the CBN Consolidated Account at the end of each banking day.
questionBank.exp: Commercial banks are mandated to remit all monies to the Consolidated Revenue Account with CBN at the end of each banking day. (Module 5, §5.13.3.3)

questionBank.q: The core banking software used by a bank for its entire operation is an example of which type of processing platform for TROPS?
questionBank.exp: The bank's Core Banking Package – e.g., Basis, Flexcube, Finacle – is the computer software selected for its entire operation. (Module 5, §5.7.3.a)

questionBank.q: A bank receives a deal slip from the Treasury Department for a placement. The TROPS officer should confirm that the counterparty:
opts: A. Has a placement line with the bank.
B. Is a member of the clearing house.
D. Is a public sector entity.
questionBank.ans: A. Has a placement line with the bank.
questionBank.exp: TROPS officer confirms that the counterparty has a placement line with the bank and that the approved line can cover the transaction. (Module 5, §5.8)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a TROPS Operations Policy requirement?
opts: A. Having no standard operating procedure.
B. Maintaining an organization chart and reporting line.
C. Allowing staff to set their own authorization limits.
D. Accepting verbal mandates from counterparties.
questionBank.ans: B. Maintaining an organization chart and reporting line.
questionBank.exp: TROPS SOP should include organization chart, roles, objectives, schedule of duties, deliverables, authorization limits, and risk acceptance criteria. (Module 5, §5.9)

questionBank.q: A bank that wants to borrow short-term funds can place Treasury Bills as collateral in an OBB transaction. This is because:
opts: A. Treasury Bills are the only acceptable collateral.
B. Treasury Bills are highly liquid and secure.
D. Treasury Bills are used for foreign exchange only.
questionBank.ans: B. Treasury Bills are highly liquid and secure.
questionBank.exp: OBB and FBB are secured by Treasury Bills, which are liquid and secure instruments. (Module 5, §5.11.3)

questionBank.q: In TROPS, the 'confirmation' stage of a transaction is important because:
opts: A. It ensures the transaction is recorded.
B. It verifies that the counterparty agrees to the terms.
C. It reduces the need for approval.
D. It allows the dealer to change the amount.
questionBank.ans: B. It verifies that the counterparty agrees to the terms.
questionBank.exp: All TROPS transactions have a confirmation stage before processing to ensure the counterparty agrees to the terms. (Module 5, §5.10.6)

questionBank.q: Under the TSA, the primary objective is to:
opts: B. Eliminate idle funds in commercial banks.
D. Reduce the number of bank accounts.
questionBank.ans: B. Eliminate idle funds in commercial banks.
questionBank.exp: The TSA helps ensure proper cash management by eliminating idle funds usually left with different commercial banks. (Module 5, §5.13.4)

questionBank.q: A TROPS officer processes an outflow for the liquidation of an inter‑bank taking. This means the bank is:
opts: A. Receiving funds from another bank.
B. Repaying funds borrowed from another bank.
C. Lending funds to another bank.
questionBank.ans: B. Repaying funds borrowed from another bank.
questionBank.exp: Outflows include liquidation of inter‑bank takings (repayment of borrowed funds). (Module 5, §5.11.2.4)

questionBank.q: A bank's Treasury Department has both front office and middle office functions. TROPS is considered part of:
questionBank.exp: TROPS serves as the processing unit and custodian of documents for treasury activities. The manual notes that TROPS functions are distinct from front office and middle office. (Module 5, §5.1.6 & §5.14.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a benefit of the Treasury Single Account?
opts: A. Increased cash holding by commercial banks.
B. Enhanced reconciliation of revenue collection and payment.
C. Reduction in CBN's oversight role.
questionBank.ans: B. Enhanced reconciliation of revenue collection and payment.
questionBank.exp: TSA enhances reconciliation of revenue collection and payment by eliminating idle funds. (Module 5, §5.13.4)

questionBank.q: A TROPS officer records deal details in deal slip registers. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: TROPS officer records deal details in deal slip registers as part of the recording function. (Module 5, §5.8)

questionBank.q: CBN T24 (now DEPO X) is an integral part of RTGS that offers services including:
opts: B. Depository, trading, transfer of money and securities, settlement, and clearing.
questionBank.ans: B. Depository, trading, transfer of money and securities, settlement, and clearing.
questionBank.exp: DEPO X offers a range of services including depository, trading, transfer of money and securities, settlement, and clearing. (Module 5, §5.7.3.c)

questionBank.q: The process of moving funds from one account to another, either within the same bank or across different banks, is called:
questionBank.exp: Funds Transfer is a process whereby funds are moved from one account to another within the branch or across branches or banks. (Module 6, §6.1.2)

questionBank.q: From a customer's perspective, which of the following is a rationale for using funds transfer services?
opts: A. Reduction in the need for bank accounts.
B. Increased risk of carrying cash.
C. Convenience and fast speed of delivery.
questionBank.ans: C. Convenience and fast speed of delivery.
questionBank.exp: Rationale from customer perspective includes convenience, reduction in cash‑carrying risks, security, fast delivery, cost efficiency, and easier settlement. (Module 6, §6.2.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a function of the Funds Transfer Unit (FTU)?
opts: A. Processing of drafts and manager's cheques.
questionBank.ans: A. Processing of drafts and manager's cheques.
questionBank.exp: FTU functions include processing drafts/manager's cheques, CBN transfers, NIBSS transfers, electronic transfers, and standing orders. (Module 6, §6.3)

questionBank.q: A customer issues a standing order instruction to transfer ₦10,000 monthly to his landlord. On the due date, the account has insufficient funds. The bank should:
opts: A. Transfer the amount and create an overdraft.
B. Notify the customer immediately that funds are insufficient.
C. Defer the transfer to the next month.
D. Charge a penalty fee and transfer the amount.
questionBank.ans: B. Notify the customer immediately that funds are insufficient.
questionBank.exp: If on due date there are no adequate funds to effect the transfer, customers should be notified immediately. (Module 6, §6.17.6)

questionBank.q: The Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system settles transactions on a:
opts: A. Net basis at the end of the day.
D. Batch basis at specific times.
questionBank.exp: Gross settlement means the transaction is settled on a one‑to‑one basis without bunching or netting with any other transaction. (Module 6, §6.9.3)

questionBank.q: Under the RTGS system, once a payment is processed, it is:
opts: A. Provisional and can be reversed.
C. Subject to the beneficiary's confirmation.
questionBank.exp: Once processed, payments are final and irrevocable under RTGS. (Module 6, §6.9.3)

questionBank.q: The NIBSS Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) system was introduced in Nigeria in:
questionBank.exp: NEFT was introduced in Nigeria in March 2004 to provide electronic payment options. (Module 6, §6.11.2)

questionBank.q: A NEFT payment instruction is irrevocable because:
opts: A. It is processed in batches.
B. The payer's bank will not accept the order if there are insufficient funds.
C. It can be reversed within 24 hours.
D. It requires the beneficiary's approval.
questionBank.ans: B. The payer's bank will not accept the order if there are insufficient funds.
questionBank.exp: A NEFT payment is irrevocable because the payer's bank simply will not accept the order if there are insufficient funds to cover it. (Module 6, §6.11.3)

questionBank.q: Bulk NEFT is typically used for which type of payment?
questionBank.exp: Bulk NEFT is used for salary payments, pension payments, dividend payments, and direct credits. (Module 6, §6.11.5.b)

questionBank.q: The NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP) system is available:
opts: B. 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
D. Only for amounts above ₦1 million.
questionBank.ans: B. 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
questionBank.exp: NIP is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. (Module 6, §6.13.2)

questionBank.q: A customer wants to transfer funds to a beneficiary in another bank after banking hours. Which system should be used?
questionBank.exp: NIP enables a customer to transfer funds instantly from his account to a beneficiary in another bank at any time of day or night. (Module 6, §6.13.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a difference between RTGS and NEFT?
opts: A. RTGS is net‑settlement based; NEFT is gross‑settlement based.
B. RTGS is gross‑settlement based; NEFT is net‑settlement based.
questionBank.ans: B. RTGS is gross‑settlement based; NEFT is net‑settlement based.
questionBank.exp: RTGS is based on gross settlement (one‑to‑one), while NEFT is based on net‑settlement (batch processing). (Module 6, §6.12)

questionBank.q: A customer uses his bank's dedicated instant payment system to transfer funds. The software is installed on his:
questionBank.exp: The bank installs the software in his mobile phone; he gets a USER ID and Password. (Module 6, §6.15.3)

questionBank.q: A standing order instruction must be:
opts: B. Written and signed by the customer.
C. Approved by the branch manager.
D. Submitted to the clearing house.
questionBank.ans: B. Written and signed by the customer.
questionBank.exp: Standing order is a written instruction given by the customer to the bank specifying an amount to be debited. (Module 6, §6.17.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a method of local funds transfer?
questionBank.exp: Local FT methods include account‑to‑account, cheques/drafts, certified cheques, RTGS/NISS, NEFT, mail transfer, in‑house clearing, and mobile transfers. (Module 6, §6.4.2)

questionBank.q: The NIBSS Automated Payment System (NAPS) commenced operations on:
questionBank.exp: NAPS commenced full operations on Monday, February 2, 2015. (Module 6, §6.14.2)

questionBank.q: NAPS is designed to facilitate:
opts: B. Electronic processing of bulk payments like salaries, pensions, and contractors.
questionBank.ans: B. Electronic processing of bulk payments like salaries, pensions, and contractors.
questionBank.exp: NAPS facilitates electronic processing of bulk payments like salaries, pensions, allowances, contractors, and direct debit recoveries. (Module 6, §6.14.3)

questionBank.q: When a customer uses Mobile Money, what is required to open a Mobile Money account?
opts: C. An account linked to his phone.
questionBank.ans: C. An account linked to his phone.
questionBank.exp: To use Mobile Money, a customer must open a Mobile Money Account linked to his phone. (Module 6, §6.16.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a service offered by Mobile Money?
opts: A. Depositing and withdrawing from an account.
questionBank.exp: Mobile Money allows deposits/withdrawals, transfers, bill payments, and airtime purchase; mortgages are not a standard Mobile Money service. (Module 6, §6.16.4)

questionBank.q: Fintech companies are defined as:
opts: A. Companies that only offer savings accounts.
B. Companies using technology to deliver financial services.
questionBank.ans: B. Companies using technology to deliver financial services.
questionBank.exp: FinTech is the technology used in delivering important financial services that were exclusive to traditional financial institutions. (Module 6, §6.18.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a major fintech company in Nigeria?
questionBank.exp: Major Fintech companies in Nigeria include Opay, Moniepoint, Kuda, PalmPay, Okash, Interswitch, Piggyvest, Paga, and Cowriewise. (Module 6, §6.18.1)

questionBank.q: The parties to a funds transfer include all of the following EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: Parties to FT are remitter, remitter's bank, beneficiary, beneficiary's bank, and intermediary (CBN, NIBSS, Discount Houses). (Module 6, §6.6)

questionBank.q: A remitter completes an application form for an RTGS transfer. The bank must first:
opts: B. Check for proper completion and verify signature.
questionBank.ans: B. Check for proper completion and verify signature.
questionBank.exp: The process: check for proper completion and verify signature, then debit the remitter's account. (Module 6, §6.9.7.2)

questionBank.q: The RTGS system is designed to handle all of the following EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: RTGS handles inter‑bank transfers, third‑party transfers, and other funds transfers; it is designed for high value transactions, not small retail POS. (Module 6, §6.9.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a goal of the RTGS system?
opts: C. To delay high value payments.
questionBank.exp: Goals include reducing settlement risk, reducing credit risk, speeding up high value payments, and giving accurate position of the bank. (Module 6, §6.9.1)

questionBank.q: A NEFT transaction initiated after the cut‑off time will be:
opts: B. Processed the next working day.
questionBank.ans: B. Processed the next working day.
questionBank.exp: A NEFT transaction initiated later than the cut off time is completed the next day. (Module 6, §6.12)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an example of a NEFT payment?
opts: C. Large inter‑bank foreign exchange settlement.
questionBank.exp: NEFT payments include utility bills, tuitions, government taxes, subscriptions, charity donations, and person‑to‑person transfers. (Module 6, §6.11.2)

questionBank.q: Under the RTGS system, participants must maintain settlement accounts with:
questionBank.exp: RTGS is a CBN initiative where all participants maintain settlement accounts with the CBN. (Module 6, §6.9.4)

questionBank.q: A standing order that is due but cannot be executed due to insufficient funds should be:
opts: A. Executed and the account overdrawn.
B. Deferred until funds are available.
D. Executed with a penalty fee.
questionBank.ans: B. Deferred until funds are available.
questionBank.exp: If funds are insufficient, the instruction cannot be executed; the customer is notified. (Module 6, §6.17.6)

questionBank.q: The NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP) requires the customer to have a:
questionBank.exp: An intending remitter applies for a Token – a User ID, User Name, and a Token. (Module 6, §6.13.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a method of foreign funds transfer?
questionBank.exp: Foreign FT methods include Travelers' cheques, foreign currency inflow, foreign bank drafts, Mail Transfer, and Western Union. (Module 6, §6.5)

questionBank.q: The primary objective of any settlement system is:
opts: B. Safety, security, soundness, effectiveness, and efficiency.
questionBank.ans: B. Safety, security, soundness, effectiveness, and efficiency.
questionBank.exp: The objectives of any settlement systems are 'safety, security, soundness, effectiveness and efficiency'. (Module 6, §6.7.3)

questionBank.q: A customer wants to transfer funds to a beneficiary in another bank using his bank's mobile app. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Mobile banking is part of the electronic payment system, which involves paperless payments using devices. (Module 6, §6.8.2)

questionBank.q: The Nigerian Inter‑Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) is owned by:
opts: A. The Central Bank of Nigeria.
questionBank.exp: NIBSS is established and owned by Banks and Discount Houses. (Module 6, §6.10.2)

questionBank.q: Under NIBSS rules, a bank's T/Bills holding must cover the amount to be transferred by at least:
questionBank.exp: The originating bank's T/Bills holding at NIBSS must cover the amount by at least 110% before transfer. (Module 6, §6.10.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a benefit of funds transfer from the banks' perspective?
questionBank.exp: From banks' perspective: source of cheap/low‑cost funds, source of fee/float income, cross‑sell products, and increase customer base. (Module 6, §6.2.2)

questionBank.q: A customer gives a written instruction to transfer funds to his daughter's account every month for school fees. This is called:
questionBank.exp: A standing order is a written instruction giving an amount to be debited periodically and transferred to a named beneficiary. (Module 6, §6.17.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following statements about mobile money is TRUE?
opts: A. It can only be used for amounts under ₦10,000.
B. It requires a linked bank account and mobile phone.
C. It is only available during banking hours.
D. It can only be used for airtime purchases.
questionBank.ans: B. It requires a linked bank account and mobile phone.
questionBank.exp: Mobile Money requires an account linked to the customer's phone and an ATM card. (Module 6, §6.16.2)

questionBank.q: A remitter uses NIP to transfer funds to a beneficiary who does not have a bank account. How can the beneficiary access the funds?
opts: A. By opening a bank account.
B. By receiving an electronic voucher and a code.
C. By visiting the remitter's bank.
questionBank.ans: B. By receiving an electronic voucher and a code.
questionBank.exp: Where the beneficiary has no mobile account, he will receive an electronic voucher on his phone and a code to claim the funds. (Module 6, §6.16.6)

questionBank.q: The major advantage of SWIFT for processing foreign currency transactions is:
questionBank.exp: SWIFT's major advantage is security for foreign currency transactions and settlements. (Module 6, §6.9.6 & Module 5, §5.7.3.d)

questionBank.q: A bank receives a funds transfer request for a beneficiary in another country. The bank should use which platform?
questionBank.exp: Foreign currency transactions and settlements are processed through SWIFT. (Module 6, §6.5)

questionBank.q: The CBN Interbank Funds Transfer (CIFT) system is now part of:
questionBank.exp: CIFT (now NISS) is an integral part of RTGS. (Module 6, §6.9)

questionBank.q: A Fintech company like Opay or Moniepoint offers services that:
opts: A. Are only available to corporate customers.
B. Make financial services easily accessible to the population.
C. Replace the need for banks entirely.
D. Are regulated by NIBSS only.
questionBank.ans: B. Make financial services easily accessible to the population.
questionBank.exp: Fintech goals include making financial services easily accessible, enhancing procedures, promoting inclusion, and ensuring seamless payments. (Module 6, §6.18.2)

questionBank.q: A customer sets up a standing order to pay his insurance premium monthly. The bank must ensure that:
opts: A. The insurance company approves the deduction.
B. The instruction is written and signed, and funds are available on due date.
C. The customer's salary is credited first.
D. The bank manager authorises each payment.
questionBank.ans: B. The instruction is written and signed, and funds are available on due date.
questionBank.exp: Standing order requires written instruction; on due date, the bank confirms funds availability and executes the transfer. (Module 6, §6.17.3-5)

questionBank.q: The Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) system is used for all of the following EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: EFT is used for direct deposits, bill payments, and online transfers; safe custody is a separate banking service. (Module 6, §7.1)

questionBank.q: Electronic banking, also known as e‑banking, can be described as an arrangement between a financial institution and its customers that allows:
opts: A. Encrypted transactions through electronic devices and telecommunications networks.
B. Unencrypted transactions through traditional paper instruments.
C. Transactions only through physical branch visits.
D. Transactions that are limited to cash deposits only.
questionBank.ans: A. Encrypted transactions through electronic devices and telecommunications networks.
questionBank.exp: E‑banking allows encrypted transactions through electronic devices and telecommunications networks. (Module 7, §7.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a service encompassed by electronic banking?
questionBank.exp: E‑banking encompasses electronic funds transfer, online banking, ATMs, telephone banking, and debit/credit cards. (Module 7, §7.1)

questionBank.q: The first online banking service was launched in which year and country?
opts: B. 1981 in the United States of America.
questionBank.ans: B. 1981 in the United States of America.
questionBank.exp: The first online banking service was launched in 1981 in the United States of America. (Module 7, §7.2)

questionBank.q: Which country has the highest number of online banking users globally?
questionBank.exp: India is the country with the highest number of online banking users, with over 150 million users. (Module 7, §7.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of electronic banking?
opts: B. Reduced need for physical bank branches.
C. Increased paperwork and manual processing.
D. Environmental benefits from reduced paper waste.
questionBank.ans: C. Increased paperwork and manual processing.
questionBank.exp: E‑banking reduces paperwork, not increases it. Benefits include convenience, speed, efficiency, cost‑effectiveness, 24/7 availability, security, personalization, and environmental benefits. (Module 7, §7.3)

questionBank.q: The most common electronic banking channel both in Nigeria and globally is:
questionBank.exp: Internet or online banking is the most common electronic banking channel in Nigeria and globally. (Module 7, §7.4.1)

questionBank.q: An ATM transaction that allows a customer to perform banking transactions without visiting a branch is an example of:
questionBank.exp: ATMs allow customers to perform several forms of banking transactions without having to visit a bank branch, making them a self‑service channel. (Module 7, §7.4.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using ATMs?
opts: D. Reduced need for bank staff.
questionBank.exp: Disadvantages of ATMs include limitations on cash withdrawals and vulnerability to physical and electronic attacks. (Module 7, §7.4.2)

questionBank.q: A customer calls the bank's contact centre to check his account balance and transfer funds. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Telephone banking allows customers to conduct transactions over the phone through the bank's contact centre. (Module 7, §7.4.3)

questionBank.q: A debit card transaction deducts funds directly from the customer's:
questionBank.exp: Debit cards deduct funds directly from the customer's bank account. (Module 7, §7.4.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a major global credit card issuing company?
questionBank.exp: The three major global credit issuing companies are Visa, Mastercard, and American Express. (Module 7, §7.4.5)

questionBank.q: Access Bank currently issues which two types of credit cards?
questionBank.exp: Access Bank currently issues Visa and American Express credit cards. (Module 7, §7.4.5)

questionBank.q: A customer uses a mobile app to transfer money to a friend, pay bills, and check his balance. This is an example of:
opts: C. Internet banking on a desktop.
questionBank.exp: Mobile banking is specifically designed for mobile devices, allowing customers to access accounts and conduct transactions through the bank's mobile app. (Module 7, §7.4.6)

questionBank.q: Access Bank's USSD code for banking services is:
questionBank.exp: Access Bank's USSD code is *901#. (Module 7, §7.4.7)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an advantage of USSD banking?
opts: B. Cost‑effectiveness and promotion of inclusive banking.
C. High security against SIM‑related fraud.
questionBank.ans: B. Cost‑effectiveness and promotion of inclusive banking.
questionBank.exp: USSD banking is convenient, cost‑effective as it does not require internet connection, and promotes inclusive banking. (Module 7, §7.4.7)

questionBank.q: An example of a P2P payment platform used for lending activities in Nigeria is:
questionBank.exp: P2P platforms like Trove and Ajobox are used mainly to carry out lending activities without the direct involvement of banks. (Module 7, §7.4.8)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a common security challenge in e‑banking?
opts: B. Security attacks and cyber threats.
questionBank.ans: B. Security attacks and cyber threats.
questionBank.exp: Security attacks are a major challenge because e‑banking channels rely on network channels vulnerable to cyberattacks. (Module 7, §7.5)

questionBank.q: A fraudster sends an email that appears to be from a bank, asking the customer to provide login details. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Phishing involves sending emails that appear to be from the bank to gain access to customer accounts. (Module 7, §7.5)

questionBank.q: The Committee of Bankers campaigns frequently to educate customers on how to:
opts: A. Increase their credit card limits.
B. Safeguard their passwords and detect fraudulent messages.
questionBank.ans: B. Safeguard their passwords and detect fraudulent messages.
questionBank.exp: The Committee of Bankers runs educational media campaigns on how to safeguard passwords and detect fraudulent messages. (Module 7, §7.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a safety tip when using electronic banking?
opts: A. Maintain strict confidentiality of personal information.
B. Use strong passwords and change them frequently.
C. Share passwords with family members for convenience.
D. Be aware of the latest scams and frauds.
questionBank.ans: C. Share passwords with family members for convenience.
questionBank.exp: Passwords should not be shared with anyone. Safety tips include confidentiality, strong passwords, awareness of scams, and contacting the bank if compromised. (Module 7, §7.7)

questionBank.q: The recommendation from the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago regarding email security is to:
opts: A. Send all sensitive data via email.
B. Ensure transmissions are encrypted before doing online transactions.
C. Avoid using email for any banking communication.
D. Use email only for sending passwords.
questionBank.ans: B. Ensure transmissions are encrypted before doing online transactions.
questionBank.exp: The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago advises making sure transmissions are encrypted before doing online transactions or sending personal information. (Module 7, §7.7)

questionBank.q: An omnichannel customer experience is defined as:
opts: A. A single channel for all banking transactions.
B. Individual customer touch points over various channels that seamlessly connect.
D. A separate experience for each banking channel.
questionBank.ans: B. Individual customer touch points over various channels that seamlessly connect.
questionBank.exp: Omnichannel is made up of individual customer touch points over a variety of channels that seamlessly connect, allowing customers to pick up transactions where they left off. (Module 7, §7.8.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an importance of omnichannel experience for banks?
opts: A. It reduces the need for technology.
B. It unites customer experience across channels.
C. It limits customers to one channel.
questionBank.ans: B. It unites customer experience across channels.
questionBank.exp: Omnichannel unites customer experience across channels, provides convenience, puts the bank in the customer's mind, and improves brand awareness. (Module 7, §7.8.2)

questionBank.q: To ensure omnichannel success, banks should introduce:
opts: A. Different login details for each channel.
B. A single sign‑on structure where the same login and password is used for all channels.
C. Separate passwords for mobile and internet banking.
questionBank.ans: B. A single sign‑on structure where the same login and password is used for all channels.
questionBank.exp: The bank must introduce a single sign‑on structure whereby the same login detail and password is used for all channels. (Module 7, §7.8.3.iv)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a strategy for migrating customers to self‑service?
opts: A. Charging higher fees for self‑service.
B. Providing positive incentives and rewards for using self‑service.
D. Making all transactions compulsory on self‑service immediately.
questionBank.ans: B. Providing positive incentives and rewards for using self‑service.
questionBank.exp: Strategies include getting staff buy‑in, advertising, providing incentives and rewards, and introducing user‑friendly self‑service points. (Module 7, §7.8.4)

questionBank.q: A customer prefers to use the branch for all transactions despite having access to digital channels. The bank's best approach is to:
opts: A. Force the customer to use digital channels.
B. Offer incentives for digital channel usage and provide education.
C. Close the branch to reduce costs.
questionBank.ans: B. Offer incentives for digital channel usage and provide education.
questionBank.exp: Strategies include incentives, awareness creation, and compulsion for certain transaction thresholds. (Module 7, §7.8.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of telephone banking?
opts: B. Ability to attend to multiple customers simultaneously.
questionBank.exp: Telephone banking has security vulnerability as a disadvantage. (Module 7, §7.4.3)

questionBank.q: A customer uses an ATM to deposit cash. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: ATMs allow customers to perform transactions without visiting a branch, making them self‑service. (Module 7, §7.4.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a benefit of using credit cards?
opts: A. Funds are deducted immediately from the bank account.
B. Easy access to credit and convenience.
questionBank.ans: B. Easy access to credit and convenience.
questionBank.exp: Advantages of credit cards include easy access to credit and convenience. Disadvantages include vulnerability to fraud and ease of overspending. (Module 7, §7.4.5)

questionBank.q: The most common security measure used for online banking is a:
questionBank.exp: The most common security measure used for online banking is a password. Two‑factor authentication is becoming increasingly popular. (Module 7, §7.2)

questionBank.q: As of December 2025, the value of global electronic banking and digital transactions reached approximately:
questionBank.exp: As of December 2025, the value of global electronic banking and digital transactions reached approximately $157 trillion. (Module 7, §7.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a strategy for migrating customers to self‑service?
opts: A. Removing all physical branch services.
B. Disincentives to customers who carry out certain transactions outside self‑service.
C. Increasing fees for digital channels.
D. Limiting transactions to only online channels.
questionBank.ans: B. Disincentives to customers who carry out certain transactions outside self‑service.
questionBank.exp: Disincentives to customers who carry out certain transactions out of self‑service is a listed strategy. (Module 7, §7.8.4)

questionBank.q: The use of OTP for certain mobile transactions can lead to delays due to:
opts: A. The customer forgetting the password.
D. The customer's phone being switched off.
questionBank.exp: In the event of network service issues, there may be a delay in concluding the transaction. (Module 7, §7.6)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a requirement for omnichannel success?
opts: A. Channels should be seen as stand‑alone entities.
B. Channels must be properly integrated for seamless handover.
C. Customers should use only one channel.
questionBank.ans: B. Channels must be properly integrated for seamless handover.
questionBank.exp: Channels must be properly integrated in such a way that hand over from one channel to another on the same transaction must be seamless. (Module 7, §7.8.3.v)

questionBank.q: A customer receives a text message from his bank with his account balance. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: SMS banking is a form of mobile banking where customers can receive text messages with account balance information, transaction alerts, and notifications. (Module 7, §7.4.7)

questionBank.q: Foreign operations in banking refer to transactions relating to:
questionBank.exp: Foreign operations are operations relating to transactions in foreign currency. (Module 8, §8.2.i)

questionBank.q: Visible transactions in foreign operations pertain to:
opts: B. Import or export of physical goods.
questionBank.ans: B. Import or export of physical goods.
questionBank.exp: Visible transactions are those pertaining to import or export of physical goods. (Module 8, §8.2.ii)

questionBank.q: Invisible transactions in foreign operations include all of the following EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: Invisible transactions are related to payment for services or travel allowances (intangible items). Importation of machinery is a visible transaction. (Module 8, §8.2.ii)

questionBank.q: A customer wants to import goods into Nigeria and needs to register the intention to import. Which document must be completed?
questionBank.exp: All import transactions are processed by completing a Form M (now electronic Form M). (Module 8, §8.2.4)

questionBank.q: The electronic Form M (E‑Form M) is a mandatory documentation process put in place by:
opts: A. The Ministry of Finance and Central Bank of Nigeria.
B. The Nigerian Customs Service only.
C. The Federal Inland Revenue Service only.
D. The Nigeria Export Promotion Council.
questionBank.ans: A. The Ministry of Finance and Central Bank of Nigeria.
questionBank.exp: The E‑Form M is a mandatory documentation process put in place by the FG through the Ministry of Finance and Central Bank of Nigeria. (Module 8, §8.3)

questionBank.q: An importer applying for an E‑Form M must first register with which agency?
opts: D. National Agency for Food and Drug Administration.
questionBank.exp: Any party importing goods into Nigeria shall register with FIRS with his or her Tax Identification Number (TIN). (Module 8, §8.3.1.1)

questionBank.q: The importer's Tax Identification Number (TIN) serves as the username to log into which portal for E‑Form M processing?
questionBank.exp: The applicant logs on to trade portal (trade.gov.ng) using his TIN as username. (Module 8, §8.3.1.1)

questionBank.q: When an importer submits an E‑Form M that indicates foreign exchange remittance will be involved, the Form M must be marked:
questionBank.exp: The Form M and supporting documents shall be clearly marked 'Valid for FOREX' or 'Not Valid for FOREX' depending on whether foreign exchange remittance is involved. (Module 8, §8.3.1.1)

questionBank.q: The BA number on an E‑Form M indicates that:
opts: A. The goods will not be inspected.
B. The goods being imported will be subjected to inspection.
C. The import is for personal effects only.
D. The import is exempt from customs duties.
questionBank.ans: B. The goods being imported will be subjected to inspection.
questionBank.exp: BA number is assigned if the goods being imported will be subjected to inspection; CB number if not. (Module 8, §8.3.1.2)

questionBank.q: An importer sends a copy of the Form M to the shipper, who must indicate the Form M number in the description column of the:
questionBank.exp: The shipper is required to indicate the Form M number in the description column of the Bill of Lading (B/L). (Module 8, §8.3.1.3)

questionBank.q: B'Odogwu is Nigeria's:
questionBank.exp: B'Odogwu is an indigenous, state‑of‑the‑art platform developed by the Nigeria Customs Service as a Unified Customs Management System. (Module 8, §8.3.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following documents must accompany an E‑Form M application?
opts: B. Pro‑forma Invoice and Insurance Certificate.
questionBank.ans: B. Pro‑forma Invoice and Insurance Certificate.
questionBank.exp: Required documents include Electronic Form M, Pro‑forma Invoice, and Insurance Certificate at 110% of Naira value. (Module 8, §8.3.3)

questionBank.q: The insurance certificate for importation must cover what percentage of the Naira value of the Form M?
questionBank.exp: The importer must insure the goods for 110% of the value of the shipment. (Module 8, §8.3.1.1)

questionBank.q: A method of payment where the buyer pays for goods before the seller produces and ships them is called:
questionBank.exp: Cash in Advance involves the buyer paying before the seller produces and ships the goods, used in markets controlled by sellers. (Module 8, §8.4 table)

questionBank.q: Which payment method is NOT allowed for import transactions in Nigeria due to past bad experiences?
questionBank.exp: Open Account is not allowed due to various bad experiences leading to debt incurred by the country. (Module 8, §8.4.1)

questionBank.q: A Letter of Credit is governed primarily by which set of rules?
questionBank.exp: Letters of Credit are governed mainly by UCP 600 (Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits). (Module 8, §8.4.2)

questionBank.q: In a Letter of Credit, the party who requests the bank to issue the credit is called the:
questionBank.exp: The Applicant is the importer or buyer who requests the credit. The Beneficiary is the exporter or seller. (Module 8, §8.4.2.1)

questionBank.q: A Letter of Credit that carries the commitment of both the confirming bank and issuing bank is called:
questionBank.exp: A Confirmed L/C carries the commitment (undertaking to pay) of both the confirming bank and the issuing bank. (Module 8, §8.4.2.2)

questionBank.q: A type of LC where a part or whole of the credit is transferred by the original beneficiary to one or more beneficiaries is called:
questionBank.exp: A Transferable L/C allows a part or whole of the credit to be transferred by the original beneficiary to one or more beneficiaries. (Module 8, §8.4.2.3)

questionBank.q: A Red Clause L/C allows for:
opts: A. Transfer of the credit to multiple beneficiaries.
B. Advance payment to the beneficiary before performance.
D. Reimbursement from the issuing bank.
questionBank.ans: B. Advance payment to the beneficiary before performance.
questionBank.exp: Red Clause L/C allows for advance payment to the beneficiary before performance under the sales contract. (Module 8, §8.4.2.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a derivative of a Letter of Credit?
questionBank.exp: Derivatives of LC include Back‑to‑Back L/C, Transferable L/C, Red Clause L/C, and Standby L/C. (Module 8, §8.4.2.3)

questionBank.q: Banks in a collection transaction act as:
questionBank.exp: Banks are only agents in collections; they are bound to follow the instructions of the principals. (Module 8, §8.4.3)

questionBank.q: Documentary Collections where documents are released to the importer only against payment are known as:
questionBank.exp: Documents against Payment (also known as Sight Collection or Cash Against Documents) requires payment before document release. (Module 8, §8.4.3.1)

questionBank.q: In Nigeria, which type of documentary collection is allowed?
opts: C. Both Documents against Payment and Acceptance.
questionBank.exp: In Nigeria, only documentary collections (against acceptance) are allowed. (Module 8, §8.4.3.2)

questionBank.q: The entity responsible for inspecting and collecting customs duties in Nigeria is the:
questionBank.exp: The Nigerian Customs Service is responsible for inspection and collection of customs revenue and anti‑smuggling efforts. (Module 8, §8.5.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a category of customs duty collected in Nigeria?
questionBank.exp: Categories include Import Duty, Excise Duty, Fees, Sugar Levy, Port Levy, VAT, Rice Levy, and ECOWAS Levy. (Module 8, §8.5.2)

questionBank.q: The PAAR (Pre‑Arrival Assessment Report) replaced the:
questionBank.exp: PAAR replaced the Risk Assessment Report (RAR) when Destination Inspection was taken over from scanning companies. (Module 8, §8.6)

questionBank.q: The PAAR is issued by which agency?
questionBank.exp: The PAAR is issued by the Nigerian Customs Service after assessment of the import documents. (Module 8, §8.6)

questionBank.q: The PAAR determines:
opts: A. The exchange rate for the import.
B. The level of inspection and all necessary levies to be paid.
C. The shipping company to be used.
D. The payment method for the import.
questionBank.ans: B. The level of inspection and all necessary levies to be paid.
questionBank.exp: PAAR determines the level of inspection and all necessary levies to be paid by the importer. (Module 8, §8.6)

questionBank.q: The HS (Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System) is created by which organization?
questionBank.exp: The HS is an international system created by the World Customs Organization for classifying traded products. (Module 8, §8.7)

questionBank.q: Goods are classified in the HS system based on:
opts: B. What they are, not their stage of fabrication or use.
questionBank.ans: B. What they are, not their stage of fabrication or use.
questionBank.exp: The HS is based on the principle that goods are classified by what they are, not according to their stage of fabrication, use, or 'made in' status. (Module 8, §8.7)

questionBank.q: Which regulatory agency is responsible for export promotion in Nigeria?
questionBank.exp: The Nigeria Export Promotion Council is responsible for export promotion. (Module 8, §8.8)

questionBank.q: Commercial exports refer to exports for which:
opts: B. The exporter expects to be paid.
C. The goods are personal effects.
questionBank.ans: B. The exporter expects to be paid.
questionBank.exp: Commercial Exports refer to exports for which the exporter expects to be paid. (Module 8, §8.9.2)

questionBank.q: The regulatory document for Commercial Export Trade processing in Nigeria is the:
questionBank.exp: The regulatory document for Commercial Export Trade processing is the E‑Form NXP. (Module 8, §8.9.2)

questionBank.q: The E‑Form NXP is valid for how long from the date of registration?
questionBank.exp: The e‑form NXP is valid for 3 years from the date of registration. (Module 8, §8.11)

questionBank.q: Export proceeds for oil exports must be repatriated within how many days of shipment?
questionBank.exp: Proceeds for Oil Export must be repatriated within 90 days of shipment. (Module 8, §8.11)

questionBank.q: Export proceeds for non‑oil exports must be repatriated within how many days of shipment?
questionBank.exp: Proceeds for Non‑Oil Export must be repatriated within 180 days of shipment. (Module 8, §8.11)

questionBank.q: Export proceeds must be received into which type of account?
questionBank.exp: Proceeds should be received into the Exporter's EXPORT PROCEEDS DOMICILIARY ACCOUNT. (Module 8, §8.15.3)

questionBank.q: The Trade Monitoring System (TRMS) is a web portal designed for the automation of:
opts: C. CBN foreign exchange trade related processes.
questionBank.ans: C. CBN foreign exchange trade related processes.
questionBank.exp: TRMS is a web portal designed for the automation of CBN foreign exchange trade related processes. (Module 8, §8.9.3)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a portal on the Trade Monitoring System (TRMS)?
questionBank.exp: The three portals are Applicant, Authorized Dealer Bank, and Other Stakeholders/MDA. (Module 8, §8.9.3)

questionBank.q: Before embarking on export business in Nigeria, an exporter must register with the:
questionBank.exp: Anyone willing to engage in commercial export business is required to register with the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC). (Module 8, §8.9.2)

questionBank.q: The Nigerian Export Supervision Scheme (NESS) levy for non‑oil exports is calculated at:
questionBank.exp: NESS fees are 0.5% of FOB value for non‑oil exports and 0.12% for oil/gas exports. (Module 8, §8.12.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is EXEMPTED from the Nigerian Export Supervision Scheme (NESS)?
opts: A. Commercial export of crude oil.
questionBank.exp: Exemptions include personal effects, used motor vehicles, day old poultry, human parts, remains, vaccines, yeast, and non‑commercial exports. (Module 8, §8.12.1)

questionBank.q: A Pre‑shipment Inspection Agent (PIA) for non‑oil exports issues which document when satisfied?
questionBank.exp: The PIA issues a Clean Certificate of Inspection (CCI) for Non‑Oil exports when satisfied. (Module 8, §8.13)

questionBank.q: For oil exports, the Pre‑shipment Inspection Agent issues a:
questionBank.exp: Provisional Certificate of Inspection (PCI) is issued for Oil Export transactions. (Module 8, §8.13)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT an approved Pre‑shipment Inspection Agent for non‑oil exports?
questionBank.exp: Globalscan is a PIA for oil exports. Non‑oil PIAs are Angelia, 8 Neroli, and Gojopal. (Module 8, §8.13.1 & §8.13.2)

questionBank.q: Effective January 8, 2025, the CBN suspended the option to:
opts: A. Use open account for imports.
B. Extend the existing repatriation timelines.
C. Issue Form M for import transactions.
D. Use Bills for Collection for exports.
questionBank.ans: B. Extend the existing repatriation timelines.
questionBank.exp: Effective January 8, 2025, CBN has suspended the option to extend the existing repatriation timelines. (Module 8, §8.15.4)

questionBank.q: Which payment method is NOT approved for export transactions in Nigeria?
questionBank.exp: Open Account is NOT an approved method of payment for export transactions in Nigeria. (Module 8, §8.16)

questionBank.q: Non‑Commercial Exports (NCX) are transactions where:
opts: A. The exporter expects to be paid.
C. The goods are inspected by PIAs.
D. The goods are subject to NESS levy.
questionBank.exp: Non‑Commercial Exports are for goods where payments are not expected. (Module 8, §8.17)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a Non‑Commercial Export transaction?
questionBank.exp: Non‑Commercial Exports include gifts/personal effects, trade samples, machinery for repairs, and supplies to diplomatic missions. (Module 8, §8.17.1)

questionBank.q: The E‑Form A is completed for which type of transaction?
questionBank.exp: The E‑Form A is completed for invisible trade transactions through the purchase of authorized foreign exchange. (Module 8, §8.18)

questionBank.q: To access the Trade Monitoring System for E‑Form A processing, an applicant must have a valid:
questionBank.exp: To access and use the system, an applicant must have a valid BVN. (Module 8, §8.18)

questionBank.q: The processing charge for an E‑Form A transaction is:
questionBank.exp: A processing charge of N5,000 is payable for E‑Form A transactions. (Module 8, §8.18)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a transaction processed using E‑Form A?
questionBank.exp: E‑Form A transactions include foreign school fees, medical bills, mortgage payments, professional subscriptions, training fees, and BTA/PTA. (Module 8, §8.18.2)

questionBank.q: A customer applying for Personal Travel Allowance (PTA) must have a valid:
opts: B. Visa of the country of destination.
questionBank.ans: B. Visa of the country of destination.
questionBank.exp: Applicants shall present a valid visa of the country of destination. (Module 8, §8.20.4)

questionBank.q: The maximum PTA/BTA entitlement per quarter is currently:
questionBank.exp: Applicants are entitled to $4,000 per quarter. (Module 8, §8.20.9)

questionBank.q: A customer applying for school fees payment must submit all of the following EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: Required documents include admission letter, invoice, student ID, and student international passport. (Module 8, §8.21)

questionBank.q: A Certificate of Capital Importation (CCI) is issued for:
opts: B. Inflow of foreign exchange or importation of machinery and equipment.
questionBank.ans: B. Inflow of foreign exchange or importation of machinery and equipment.
questionBank.exp: CCI is issued for inflows of foreign exchange and importation of machinery and equipment or raw materials. (Module 8, §8.26)

questionBank.q: To issue a CCI for inflow of foreign exchange, the funds must be sold within:
questionBank.exp: Such funds must be sold within 24 hours. (Module 8, §8.26.1)

questionBank.q: The Electronic Certificate of Capital Importation (eCCI) was implemented by CBN in:
questionBank.exp: CBN announced the implementation of eCCI in September 2017. (Module 8, §8.26.1)

questionBank.q: A domiciliary account is an account maintained in:
opts: D. Both Naira and foreign currency.
questionBank.exp: Domiciliary accounts are in different currency types such as US Dollars, Pound Sterling, or Euros. (Module 8, §3.7.13.2)

questionBank.q: For a foreign cheque deposited for clearing through a correspondent bank, the proceeds can be used for:
questionBank.exp: Proceeds can be used for offshore payments (Telegraphic transfers), FX draft requests, or withdrawn as cash. (Module 8, §8.25.1.3)

questionBank.q: A customer receives funds from an offshore correspondent bank into his domiciliary account. The bank must ensure that:
opts: A. The funds are converted to Naira immediately.
B. The full amount is credited to the beneficiary's account.
C. The funds are held for 24 hours before crediting.
D. The customer provides a Board Resolution.
questionBank.ans: B. The full amount is credited to the beneficiary's account.
questionBank.exp: The full amount received should be credited to the account of the receiving bank and in turn to the beneficiary. (Module 8, §8.24.1.3)

questionBank.q: For a domiciliary outflow, the customer's transfer instruction must include:
questionBank.exp: The purpose of payment on the transfer instruction must be acceptable (e.g., Payment for Services, Upkeep Allowance). (Module 8, §8.24.2.2.b)

questionBank.q: The objective of completing the E‑Form NXP is to ensure all of the following EXCEPT:
opts: A. Goods meet the buyer's expectation.
B. Only goods that satisfied the order have been shipped.
C. Proceeds are repatriated within 90/180 days.
D. The exporter is registered with the Nigeria Export Promotion Council.
questionBank.ans: D. The exporter is registered with the Nigeria Export Promotion Council.
questionBank.exp: The objectives are to ensure goods meet expectations, only satisfied goods are shipped, and proceeds are repatriated. Registration with NEPC is a prerequisite, not an objective of the form. (Module 8, §8.11)

questionBank.q: Fraud can be defined as an act of deception intentionally practiced to secure:
questionBank.exp: Fraud is a deception deliberately practiced to secure unfair or unlawful gain, involving dishonesty, theft, manipulation, or abuse of office. (Module 9, §9.1)

questionBank.q: A person who intentionally misrepresents a material fact so that someone else parts with property or surrenders a right is called a:
questionBank.exp: A fraudster intentionally misrepresents a material fact so that someone else acting on it will part with property or surrender a right. (Module 9, §9.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a personality that can perpetrate fraud in a bank?
opts: A. Employees of the bank only.
C. Customers, employees, management, and external actors.
questionBank.ans: C. Customers, employees, management, and external actors.
questionBank.exp: Frauds can be perpetrated by employees, management, customers, or external actors exploiting vulnerabilities. (Module 9, §9.2.1)

questionBank.q: A person uses fake documents to obtain a bank loan and disappears without repaying. This is an example of which fraud feature?
questionBank.exp: Deception is the act of getting what does not belong to you by false pretenses, such as using fake documents. (Module 9, §9.3 table)

questionBank.q: An employee of a bank misappropriates customer cash entrusted for deposit into the customer's account. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Breach of confidence involves disappointing and fraudulent activities of trusted persons, such as misappropriating customer funds. (Module 9, §9.3 table)

questionBank.q: A branch manager uses the bank's official pool car for personal purposes without authorisation. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Impropriety is the abuse of office or betrayal of confidence by trusted officials, such as misusing bank assets. (Module 9, §9.3 table)

questionBank.q: The theory that explains the reasons behind a worker's decision to commit workplace fraud is called the:
questionBank.exp: The Fraud Triangle, propounded by Donald R. Cressey and Edwin Sutherland, explains the reasons behind workplace fraud. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a component of the Fraud Triangle?
questionBank.exp: The Fraud Triangle consists of three components: Pressure (or Incentive), Opportunity, and Rationalisation. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: A teller steals cash from the vault because he is overwhelmed by debt from medical bills. This motive falls under which Fraud Triangle component?
questionBank.exp: Pressure (or Incentive) relates to motivation for committing fraud, which may result from financial hardship or personal stress. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: A bank employee justifies stealing money by thinking 'I was only borrowing it and will pay it back'. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Rationalisation is the justification that unethical behaviour is something other than criminal activity, such as 'I was only borrowing the money'. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: Weak internal controls and lack of management oversight create which component of the Fraud Triangle?
questionBank.exp: Opportunity is created by ineffective control or governance systems that allow an individual to commit organizational fraud. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: According to research, approximately what percentage of fraud cases are influenced by financial pressure?
questionBank.exp: About 95% of all cases of fraud have been influenced by financial pressure resulting from personal, employment stress, and external pressure. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a fraud‑prone activity in the Cash & Teller Unit?
opts: D. Account opening for unknown clients.
questionBank.exp: Cash & Teller fraud‑prone activities include cash shortage, forged instruments/mandates, cash movements crime, vault manipulation, and counterfeit. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Which department is most associated with fraud involving fake or wrong account opening documents?
questionBank.exp: Customer Service fraud‑prone activities include fake or wrong account opening documents, abuse of waivers/deferrals, and dormant account fraud. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Cheque cloning and suppression of instruments are fraud‑prone activities associated with which department?
questionBank.exp: Clearing Operations fraud‑prone activities include cheque cloning, suppression of instruments, payment of incomplete cheques, collusion, and cheque kiting. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: A fraudster gains unauthorised access to a bank's database through a stolen password. This is a fraud‑prone activity in which department?
questionBank.exp: IT fraud‑prone activities include unauthorised access, stolen passwords, unrestricted access to database, data corruption, and cyber attacks. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Creating fictitious deposit accounts and collusion between treasury dealers are fraud‑prone activities in which department?
questionBank.exp: Treasury/TROPS fraud‑prone activities include creating fictitious deposits, collusion with depositors or dealers, and unauthorised fund placements. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Which type of fraud involves sending fraudulent emails that appear to be from a bank to obtain personal information?
questionBank.exp: Phishing is a form of electronic banking fraud where fraudsters send emails appearing to be from the bank to obtain sensitive information. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Skimming as a type of fraud involves:
opts: B. Stealing card information at ATMs or POS terminals.
questionBank.ans: B. Stealing card information at ATMs or POS terminals.
questionBank.exp: Skimming is a fraud technique where card information is stolen at ATMs or POS terminals. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a reason why banks are vulnerable to fraud?
opts: A. Banks hold small amounts of assets.
B. The increasing shift to digital banking has eliminated risks.
C. Banks hold vast amounts of money, making them attractive targets.
D. Banking products have become simpler.
questionBank.ans: C. Banks hold vast amounts of money, making them attractive targets.
questionBank.exp: Banks hold vast amounts of money and assets, making them attractive targets. Other vulnerabilities include digital technology, complexity, data compromise, and sophisticated criminal techniques. (Module 9, §9.7)

questionBank.q: The interoperability of banks and third‑party vendors can create fraud vulnerability because:
opts: B. It creates security vulnerabilities if partners have inadequate measures.
C. It eliminates the need for internal controls.
questionBank.ans: B. It creates security vulnerabilities if partners have inadequate measures.
questionBank.exp: Interoperability may give rise to security vulnerabilities if third‑party partners have inadequate security measures. (Module 9, §9.7.8)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an effect or impact of fraud on a bank?
opts: C. Loss of confidence by shareholders.
questionBank.ans: C. Loss of confidence by shareholders.
questionBank.exp: Effects include income loss, loss of tax revenue, loss of confidence by shareholders, loss of patronage, shock and trauma, surveillance, image problems, and being contagious. (Module 9, §9.8)

questionBank.q: Fraud Risk Management strategies are classified into three categories:
questionBank.exp: The three categories are Preventive (proactive measures to stop fraud), Detective (mechanisms to identify fraud), and Corrective (strategies to mitigate impact and prevent recurrence). (Module 9, §9.9)

questionBank.q: Segregation of duties and authorisation procedures are examples of which type of fraud control?
questionBank.exp: Preventive controls include segregation of duties, authorisation procedures, access controls, employee training, and cybersecurity measures. (Module 9, §9.9.1)

questionBank.q: Data analytics, machine learning, and anomaly detection software are used for which type of fraud control?
questionBank.exp: Detective controls use technology tools such as data analytics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and anomaly detection to identify potential fraud. (Module 9, §9.9.2)

questionBank.q: Real‑time monitoring of transactions is an example of which fraud control category?
questionBank.exp: Fraud detection systems are designed to operate in real‑time to identify and respond to fraudulent activities promptly. (Module 9, §9.9.2)

questionBank.q: Investigating fraud incidents, recovering losses, and sanctioning wrongdoers are examples of which type of fraud control?
questionBank.exp: Corrective (or response) involves investigation, remediation, recovery, sanctioning, and strengthening controls to prevent recurrence. (Module 9, §9.9.3)

questionBank.q: A bank employee colludes with a customer to defraud the bank by approving a fictitious loan. This is an example of fraud in which department?
questionBank.exp: Credit/Marketing fraud includes collusion with customers to defraud, manipulation of customer accounts, booking fictitious loans, and manipulation of rates. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an example of sharp practices as a fraud feature?
opts: A. A person uses fake documents to obtain a loan.
B. A bank IT staff exploits system knowledge to transfer funds.
C. A branch manager uses the bank's pool car for personal use.
D. A person lies about their identity to withdraw someone else's money.
questionBank.ans: B. A bank IT staff exploits system knowledge to transfer funds.
questionBank.exp: Sharp practices involve the wrong use of knowledge or skill to gain undue advantage, such as exploiting system knowledge. (Module 9, §9.3 table)

questionBank.q: Financial Statement fraud involves all of the following EXCEPT:
opts: B. Collusion with a depositor to defraud the bank.
questionBank.exp: Financial Statement fraud involves creating fictitious deposits, collusion with depositors, and collusion between treasury dealers. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a common fraud technique in Information Technology?
opts: C. Data corruption for unlawful motive.
questionBank.ans: C. Data corruption for unlawful motive.
questionBank.exp: IT fraud includes unauthorised access, stolen passwords, unrestricted access, manipulation of programs, data corruption, and cyber attacks. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: A fraudster gains access to a customer's account by tricking the customer into revealing their password. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Social engineering involves tricking individuals into revealing sensitive information or performing actions that compromise security. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: The opportunity component of the Fraud Triangle can be diminished by:
opts: B. Implementing effective internal control procedures.
questionBank.ans: B. Implementing effective internal control procedures.
questionBank.exp: Internal control procedures can particularly diminish the 'opportunity' point of the Fraud Triangle. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: A fraudster justifies his actions by thinking 'I was underpaid and my employer had cheated me'. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Rationalisation includes justifications such as 'I was underpaid/my employer had cheated me'. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: Phishing, skimming, and identity theft are types of fraud associated with which area of banking?
questionBank.exp: Electronic banking fraud includes identity theft, phishing, skimming, trojans, malware, and social engineering. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: A bank employee suppresses cash or cheques received from customers. This is a fraud‑prone activity in which unit?
questionBank.exp: Suppression of cash/cheque is listed as a fraudulent practice in Cash & Teller operations. (Module 9, §9.4)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a type of bank fraud?
questionBank.exp: Unauthorised withdrawals through ATMs are listed as a type of fraudulent practice. (Module 9, §9.4.1)

questionBank.q: Fraudulent liquidation of fixed deposits is an example of fraud in which area?
questionBank.exp: Fraudulent liquidation of fixed deposits is listed under fraudulent practices in banks. (Module 9, §9.4.7)

questionBank.q: The 'tone at the top' refers to management's attitude towards:
questionBank.exp: Weak internal controls and lack of management oversight/tone at the top contribute to opportunity for fraud. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: Which fraud control measure involves educating employees about fraud risks and ethical standards?
questionBank.exp: Employee awareness about fraud risks, ethical standards, and reporting procedures is a key component of fraud prevention. (Module 9, §9.9.1)

questionBank.q: When a fraud is detected, the investigation and remediation phase falls under which category?
questionBank.exp: Corrective includes investigation, remediation, recovery, and strengthening controls after fraud is detected. (Module 9, §9.9.3)

questionBank.q: A bank that fails to conduct due diligence on a third‑party vendor exposes itself to fraud vulnerability because:
opts: A. Third‑party vendors always have strong controls.
B. Interoperability may create security vulnerabilities.
C. Third‑party vendors are not regulated.
D. Due diligence is not required for vendors.
questionBank.ans: B. Interoperability may create security vulnerabilities.
questionBank.exp: Interoperability of banks and third‑party vendors may give rise to security vulnerabilities if partners have inadequate security measures. (Module 9, §9.7.8)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a fraudulent practice involving General Ledgers?
opts: A. Fraudulent debit of General Ledgers.
B. Proper reconciliation of General Ledgers.
questionBank.ans: A. Fraudulent debit of General Ledgers.
questionBank.exp: Fraudulent debit of General Ledgers is listed as a fraudulent practice in banks. (Module 9, §9.4.6)

questionBank.q: A customer complains that someone has taken over his account and made unauthorised withdrawals. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Account takeover is a type of electronic banking fraud where an unauthorised person gains control of a customer's account. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: The first step in preventing fraud is to:
opts: A. Conduct investigations after fraud occurs.
B. Conduct risk assessments to identify vulnerabilities.
questionBank.ans: B. Conduct risk assessments to identify vulnerabilities.
questionBank.exp: Fraud prevention starts with risk assessment to identify potential vulnerabilities and weak points in systems, processes, and controls. (Module 9, §9.9.1)

questionBank.q: A bank employee knowingly approves a loan for a customer who does not meet the requirements, in exchange for a bribe. This is an example of:
questionBank.exp: Collusion involves working together with customers or others to defraud the bank. (Module 9, §9.2.1 & §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a fraud control strategy that aims to mitigate the impact and prevent future occurrences?
questionBank.exp: Corrective controls include analyzing root causes, implementing corrective actions, and enhancing fraud prevention measures. (Module 9, §9.9.3)

questionBank.q: A bank's fraud detection system generates an alert for an unusually large transaction. The bank's response should be to:
opts: A. Approve the transaction as it may be legitimate.
questionBank.exp: When suspicious activities are detected, fraud detection systems generate alerts to notify stakeholders for investigation. (Module 9, §9.9.2)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a potential consequence of fraud for a bank?
questionBank.exp: Effects include surveillance by regulatory authorities. (Module 9, §9.8.6)

questionBank.q: A bank employee shares their password with a colleague to help with workload. This creates fraud vulnerability because:
opts: A. The colleague may be more efficient.
B. It violates password security and enables unauthorised access.
C. It is encouraged by management.
D. It reduces the need for supervision.
questionBank.ans: B. It violates password security and enables unauthorised access.
questionBank.exp: Stolen passwords and unrestricted access to databases are fraud vulnerabilities in IT. (Module 9, §9.6 table & §9.7)

questionBank.q: The 'pressure' component of the Fraud Triangle can include all of the following EXCEPT:
questionBank.exp: Pressure relates to motivation from financial hardship, employment stress, or personal stress. Strong controls reduce opportunity, not pressure. (Module 9, §9.5)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a fraud‑prone activity in Financial Control/General Administration?
questionBank.exp: Financial Control/Gen Admin fraud includes abuse of capital expenses, abuse of operating expenses, and unauthorised use of bank assets. (Module 9, §9.6 table)

questionBank.q: A bank's failure to implement robust cybersecurity measures creates vulnerability to which type of fraud?
opts: C. Cyber fraud and data breaches.
questionBank.ans: C. Cyber fraud and data breaches.
questionBank.exp: Digital security is a key component of fraud prevention; lack of cybersecurity measures creates vulnerability to cyber fraud and data breaches. (Module 9, §9.9.1)

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a correct statement about fraud correction (response)?
opts: A. It focuses only on prevention.
B. It involves reactive response to identified fraud.
C. It does not involve legal actions.
D. It ignores root cause analysis.
questionBank.ans: B. It involves reactive response to identified fraud.
questionBank.exp: Fraud correction involves reactive response to identified fraud, including investigation, remediation, legal actions, and enhancement of controls. (Module 9, §9.9.3)

questionBank.q: The ultimate goal of fraud risk management is to:
opts: B. Protect the bank's assets and reputation while minimizing fraud risk.
questionBank.ans: B. Protect the bank's assets and reputation while minimizing fraud risk.
questionBank.exp: Fraud risk management aims to protect the bank's assets and reputation, prevent fraud, detect it early, and respond effectively to minimize impact. (Module 9, §9.9)
